dervis-irab:24-28.t:
* I'rab:
(أَفَمَنْ يَتَّقِي بِوَجْهِهِ سُوءَ الْعَذابِ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ) The hamza is for a resumptive, rhetorical denial (istiʾnāf inkārī), and the fāʾ is a conjunction attached to an implied clause understood from the content of the context, that is: "Are all people equal? So is he who guards himself…". مَنْ is a relative noun in the position of the nominative, a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause يتقي بوجهه is its ṣila (relative clause); سوء العذاب is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); يوم القيامة is an adverbial attached to يتقي; and the khabar (predicate) of مَنْ is omitted, its implied form being "like him who is safe from the punishment". The meaning of guarding oneself with the face will come in the section on Rhetoric.
(وَقِيلَ لِلظَّالِمِينَ ذُوقُوا ما كُنْتُمْ تَكْسِبُونَ) وقيل is conjoined to يتقي, that is: "and it will be said to them: Taste…". The past tense was used instead to indicate that the saying is certain to occur. It is also permissible for the wāw to be circumstantial (ḥāl), the clause then being in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from the pronoun in يتقي. للظالمين is attached to قيل; here the overt noun is put in place of the pronoun in order to record the wrongdoing against them. The clause ذوقوا is the content of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ما is the mafʿūl bihi of ذوقوا; كنتم تكسبون is kāna with its noun and predicate, and the clause is the ṣila of ما.
(كَذَّبَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ فَأَتاهُمُ الْعَذابُ مِنْ حَيْثُ لا يَشْعُرُونَ) A resumptive statement, brought to explain what befell the disbelievers before them of worldly punishment. كذب الذين is a verb and agent; من قبلهم is attached to an omitted element which is the ṣila of الذين. فأتاهم العذاب is conjoined to what precedes: أتاهم is a verb with a fronted direct object, and العذاب is a postponed agent. من حيث «[Translator's note: the source prints «من حييث», a typographical slip for «من حيث»]» is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to أتاهم, and the clause لا يشعرون is in the position of the genitive, being the muḍāf ilayhi of the adverb.
(فَأَذاقَهُمُ اللَّهُ الْخِزْيَ فِي الْحَياةِ الدُّنْيا) The fāʾ is a conjunction; أذاقهم الله is a verb with a fronted direct object and a postponed agent; الخزي is a second direct object; في الحياة الدنيا is attached to أذاقهم or to an omitted element as a ḥāl. (وَلَعَذابُ الْآخِرَةِ أَكْبَرُ لَوْ كانُوا يَعْلَمُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction and the lām is the lām of ibtidāʾ (commencement); عذاب الآخرة is a mubtadaʾ and أكبر its khabar; لو is conditional; كان with its noun, and the clause يعلمون is its predicate. The apodosis of لو is omitted, indicated by what precedes, and the object of يعلمون is also omitted, its implied form being "its punishment". (وَلَقَدْ ضَرَبْنا لِلنَّاسِ فِي هذَا الْقُرْآنِ مِنْ كُلِّ مَثَلٍ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction and the lām is the answer to an omitted oath; ضربنا is a verb and agent; للناس is attached to ضربنا, as a second direct object, because ضرب includes the meaning of "to make"; في هذا القرآن is a ḥāl; من كل مثل is an adjective of the first direct object of ضربنا, i.e. "a parable taken from every parable"; لعل with its noun, and the clause يتذكرون is its predicate.
(قُرْآناً عَرَبِيًّا غَيْرَ ذِي عِوَجٍ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَّقُونَ) قرآنا is a ḥāl muwaṭṭiʾa (a "paving" circumstantial), since it is mentioned as a preliminary to the adjective, which is a derived form, while it itself is a non-derived noun; it is a ḥāl from القرآن, and the reliance in it is on the adjective. al-Laqqānī said: «قرآنا is a maṣdar meaning "reading", so it is interpreted as "something read, Arabic", and it is thus a maṣdar, and a maṣdar used as ḥāl is interpreted as a derived form.» al-Ṣafāqusī said: «It is said that the ḥāl is قرآنا and عربيا is the preliminary; the meaning of "preliminary" is that when a non-derived noun is described with something that may be a ḥāl, it becomes fit to be a ḥāl.» On this basis one vocalizes موطّأة with a fatḥa on the ṭāʾ. al-Samīn said: «The third: that it be accusative as a ḥāl from القرآن, as an emphatic ḥāl, and it is called a ḥāl muwaṭṭiʾa because the ḥāl in reality is عربيا and قرآنا is a preliminary to it, as in "Zayd came as a righteous man".» Thus al-Zamakhsharī determined it. al-Zamakhsharī and others permitted that قرآنا be accusative as praise (madḥ), because, being indefinite, it cannot follow القرآن as a dependent; and Abū l-Baqāʾ permitted it to be accusative by يتذكرون.
وغير ذي عوج is a second adjective of قرآنا (its meaning will come in the section on Rhetoric); and لعلهم يتقون: لعل with its noun, and the clause يتقون is its predicate.

* Rhetoric:
1- Kināya (metonymy) or majāz tamthīlī (representative figurative usage):
In His saying «أفمن يتقي بوجهه سوء العذاب» there is a kināya for not guarding oneself at all, because the face is not what one guards with; what one guards with is the two hands, and these are bound. Had they not been bound, he would have warded off [the fire] from the face with them, since it is the most precious of his limbs. It is also said that it is a majāz tamthīlī, because the one cast into the Fire did not intend to guard himself with his face, but found nothing other than his face with which to guard against the Fire, and had he found it he would have done so; so when he met it with his face, his state was the state of one guarding himself with his face, and this was expressed as "guarding", by way of majāz tamthīlī, which is also beautiful. al-Nābigha said:
سقط النصيف ولم تردوا إسقاطه ... فتناولته واتقتنا باليد (The veil fell and she did not mean to drop it; so she picked it up and shielded herself from us with her hand.)
2- The meaning of ʿiwaj:
The meaning of العوج was given in [Sūrat] al-Kahf: that ʿiwaj with a kasra is specific to abstract meanings rather than to concrete things, and the secret in this; refer to it there. It is also said that what is meant by ʿiwaj is doubt and confusion. The poet said:
وقد أتاك يقين غير ذي عوج ... من الإله وقول غير مكذوب (Certainty has come to you, with no crookedness, from the Deity, and a saying that is not falsified.)
In any case, the speech contains an istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya (explicit metaphor).

dervis-irab:29-32.t:
* Vocabulary:
(مُتَشاكِسُونَ): quarrelling, differing. al-Zamakhsharī said: «التشاكس and التشاخس mean disagreement; you say: تشاكست أحواله (his conditions were at odds) and تشاخست أسنانه (his teeth were uneven).» In al-Mukhtār: «رجل شكس (on the pattern of فلس) means a man of difficult character; and قوم شكس (on the pattern of قفل); its verb pattern is سلم. al-Farrāʾ reported شكس with a kasra on the kāf, and that is the regular form. I say: His saying the Exalted "in which are partners متشاكسون" means differing, of difficult characters» «[Translator's note: the source prints «عسرو الأخلاق», «عسرو» appears to be a misprint, probably for «عسرى»; translated as "of difficult characters"]». In al-Ṣiḥāḥ: «رجل شكس, with sukūn, means a man of difficult character, and قوم شكس like رجل صدق and قوم صدق; and شكس with a kasra, from the pattern سلم, means to be difficult in character, noun شكاسة. al-Farrāʾ reported: رجل شكس with a kasra on the kāf, and that is the regular form.»
When shīn and sīn are the first and last radicals of a word, they characteristically convey hardness, refusal and bad character. One says شئس (like فرح) meaning hard, so he is شئس and شأس. الشحس (with fatḥa) is a tree like the ʿatam but taller, from which bows are not made because of its dryness. الشخس is agitation and disagreement, as has preceded. الشرس (with vowels on its letters) is bad character and extreme opposition, like الشراسة; الأشرس is the bold one in fighting, and the lion; and "this is a camel not yet tamed" is هذا جمل لم يشرس. الشس is hard ground as if a single rock. الشطس is cunning and knowledge of it; الشطسي (like جمحيّ) is the formidable, rebellious, shrewd man. الشمس is well known, and nothing is more unyielding than it; and شمس الفرس شموسا وشماسا means the horse refused its back [to the rider], so it is شامس and شموس. الشموس is also wine, because it makes its drinker shamūs. الشموس (with vowels) is looking with the corner of the eye out of arrogance or rage, like التشاوس. This is among the rare features of our noble language.
(سَلَماً): the maṣdar of سلم. It was also read سالما as an active participle, meaning "pure".

* I'rab:
(ضَرَبَ اللَّهُ مَثَلًا رَجُلًا فِيهِ شُرَكاءُ مُتَشاكِسُونَ وَرَجُلًا سَلَماً لِرَجُلٍ هَلْ يَسْتَوِيانِ مَثَلًا) A resumptive statement, brought to illustrate the one who worships many gods and the one who worships one God. ضرب الله is a verb and agent; مثلا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); رجلا is a badal (substitute) for مثلا, and a parallel parsing has already been given. al-Kisāʾī said: رجلا is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. "a parable concerning a man". فيه is a fronted khabar, شركاء a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is an adjective of رجلا; متشاكسون is an adjective (naʿt) of شركاء. ورجلا is conjoined to رجلا; سلما is an adjective in the form of a maṣdar, for emphasis; لرجل is attached to the maṣdar. هل is an interrogative particle; يستويان is an imperfect verb with its agent; مثلا is a tamyīz (specification) converted from the agent, i.e. "their likeness is not equal". The specification was put in the singular because it was confined to it in the first instance. It was also read مثلين, to match the states of the two men.
(الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ بَلْ أَكْثَرُهُمْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ) الحمد is a mubtadaʾ and لله its khabar; the nominal clause is parenthetical, because His saying «بل أكثرهم لا يعلمون» is a transitional iḍrāb (turning away) connected to His saying «هل يستويان». أكثرهم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause لا يعلمون its khabar.
(إِنَّكَ مَيِّتٌ وَإِنَّهُمْ مَيِّتُونَ) A resumptive clause, brought to answer them; they had been waiting for his death and thinking it slow in coming, so Allah the Exalted informed [them] that death comes to all of them together, so there is no sense in waiting and impatience, nor any justification for gloating over one who is himself perishing. إنك ميت: inna with its noun and khabar; وإنهم ميتون is conjoined to what precedes. More will be said on this verse in the section on Rhetoric. (ثُمَّ إِنَّكُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ عِنْدَ رَبِّكُمْ تَخْتَصِمُونَ) ثم is a conjunction of sequence with delay; inna with its noun; يوم القيامة is an adverbial attached to يختصمون; عند ربكم is an adverbial attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl. The meaning of الاختصام will come in the section on Benefits. (فَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّنْ كَذَبَ عَلَى اللَّهِ وَكَذَّبَ بِالصِّدْقِ إِذْ جاءَهُ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; مَنْ is an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative, a mubtadaʾ, whose meaning is negation, i.e. "no one"; ممن is attached to أظلم; the clause كذب على الله is the ṣila of مَن; وكذب بالصدق is conjoined to كذب على الله; إذ جاءه is an adverbial attached to كذب بالصدق, i.e. he denied the Qur'an at the time of its coming; the clause جاءه is in the position of the genitive, being the muḍāf ilayhi of the adverb.
(أَلَيْسَ فِي جَهَنَّمَ مَثْوىً لِلْكافِرِينَ) The hamza is for an affirmative interrogative (istifhām taqrīrī); ليس is a defective past verb; في جهنم is its fronted khabar; مثوى is its postponed noun; للكافرين is an adjective of مثوى, or is attached to مثوى itself, because it is a noun of place from ثوى, "to dwell".

* Rhetoric:
1- The art of the proverb (fann al-mathal):
In His saying «ضرب الله مثلا رجلا فيه شركاء» to the end of the verse is the art of the circulated proverb. He likened the state of one who worships various gods to a slave owned jointly by partners among whom bitter dispute and open quarrelling have arisen; they pull him this way and that and take turns using him for their various purposes and conflicting desires, so he stands bewildered, not knowing to which of them to turn, which of them to obey, and which of them is most deserving of his obedience. And [He likened] the state of one who worships one God to one wholly devoted to his service, who meets all his needs and listens attentively to everything he is charged with and asked to do.
2- The difference between mayyit and mayt:
al-Farrāʾ said: «الميّت with shadda is one who has not yet died but will die; and الميْت with sukūn is one from whom the soul has departed.» For that reason it was not given the light form in the verse, because he had not yet died, and they had not yet died, relative to the time of the verse's revelation. al-Zamakhsharī said: «The difference between الميت and المائت is that الميت is a permanent attribute like السيد, while المائت is a newly occurring form: you say "Zayd is māʾit tomorrow", as you say "sāʾid tomorrow", meaning he will die and he will become a leader. And when you say "Zayd is mayyit", it is like saying ḥayy for its opposite, in terms of permanence and fixity. The meaning of «إنك ميت وإنهم ميتون» is that you and they, though alive, are counted among the dead, because what is bound to be is as if it had already happened.»

* Benefits:
This is a short passage whose inclusion is unavoidable concerning the meaning of الاختصام. It is reported on the authority of ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Zubayr that he said: When [the verse] «ثم إنكم يوم القيامة عند ربكم تختصمون» was revealed, al-Zubayr said: "O Messenger of Allah, will we have a dispute, after what there was between us in this world?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then the matter is indeed severe." al-Tirmidhī recorded it and said: a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ ḥadīth. Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: We lived a stretch of time thinking that this verse, «ثم إنكم يوم القيامة عند ربكم تختصمون», was revealed concerning the People of the two Books. We said: "How can we dispute, when our religion is one and our Prophet is one? What is this dispute?" Then on the day of Ṣiffīn, when some of us charged at others with swords, we said: "Yes, this is it."
On the authority of Abū Bakra, he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: «When two Muslims confront each other with their swords, the killer and the killed are both in the Fire.» al-Qasṭallānī said in his commentary: that is, each of them strikes the other, when their fighting is without any [valid] interpretation but out of worldly enmity or the seeking of kingship, for example. As for one who fights the rebels or repels an assailant and is killed, no. And if the two are Companions, their matter was based on ijtihād for the reform of the religion. It also indicates that whoever resolves on a sin is sinful even if he does not commit it. In another narration: «When one Muslim raises a weapon against his brother, they are both on the edge of Hell, and if one kills his companion, both enter it.» He said: We said, or it was said: "O Messenger of Allah, this is the killer, but what of the killed?" He said: «He wanted to kill his companion.» Narrated by al-Bukhārī and Muslim. The scholars said: the meaning of their being in the Fire is that they deserve it, but their matter is with Allah the Exalted: if He wills He punishes them and then brings them out of the Fire like the rest of the monotheists, and if He wills He pardons them and does not punish them at all. It is also said that it applies to one who deems that permissible. The majority of the Companions and Successors held that it is obligatory to support the truth and to fight the rebels. The people of the Sunna agreed on the obligation to refrain from criticizing any of the Companions for what occurred among them, even if the one in the right among them is known, because they fought in those wars only out of ijtihād, and Allah the Exalted has pardoned the one who errs in ijtihād; indeed it is established that he receives one reward, and the one who is correct two rewards. These [scholars] applied the threat mentioned in the ḥadīth to one who fights without a sound interpretation, merely seeking kingship.
al-Bazzār recorded in the ḥadīth «The killer and the killed are in the Fire» an addition that makes the meaning clear: «When you fight one another over worldly gain, the killer and the killed are in the Fire.» This is supported by what Muslim recorded in these words: «The world will not pass away until a time comes upon people when the killer does not know why he killed nor the killed why he was killed. It was said: How can that be? He said: Al-harj: the killer and the killed are in the Fire.» This is all that can be said here; the discussion in this chapter is long and is to be pursued in the larger works, since it lies outside the scope of this book.

dervis-irab:1-3.t:
* I'rab:
تَنْزِيلُ الْكِتابِ مِنَ اللَّهِ الْعَزِيزِ الْحَكِيمِ) [Translator's note: the opening parenthesis is missing in the source.] (تنزيل) is mubtadaʾ; (الكتاب) is its muḍāf ilayhi; (من الله) is the khabar; and (العزيز الحكيم) are two adjectives. (تنزيل) may also be the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, that is, "this is a revelation". (من الله) is attached to the maṣdar, or to an omitted word as a khabar after a khabar, or to an omitted word as a ḥāl from (الكتاب).
(إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنا إِلَيْكَ الْكِتابَ بِالْحَقِّ) (إن) and its subject; the clause (أنزلنا) is its khabar. The sentence is resumptive, to explain the one to whom it was sent down and what follows upon its descent. (إليك) is attached to (أنزلنا); (الكتاب) is a direct object; and (بالحق) is a ḥāl from the agent or the object, that is, "both being joined with the truth" or "it being joined with the truth".
(فَاعْبُدِ اللَّهَ مُخْلِصاً لَهُ الدِّينَ) The (فاء) is the eloquent (fāʾ al-faṣīḥa); (اعبد الله) is an imperative verb, a latent agent and a direct object; (مخلصا) is a ḥāl; (له) is attached to (مخلصا); and (الدين) is a direct object.
(أَلا لِلَّهِ الدِّينُ الْخالِصُ) A resumptive statement confirming what precedes. (ألا) is a particle of alerting and opening; (لله) is the fronted khabar; (الدين) is the deferred mubtadaʾ; and (الخالص) is an adjective.
(وَالَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِهِ أَوْلِياءَ ما نَعْبُدُهُمْ إِلَّا لِيُقَرِّبُونا إِلَى اللَّهِ زُلْفى) (والذين): the (واو) is resumptive; (الذين) is mubtadaʾ; the clause (اتخذوا) is the ṣila of the relative; (من دونه) is a ḥāl or a second direct object; (أولياء) is the first direct object; and the clause (ما نعبدهم) is the object of an omitted saying which is the khabar of (الذين), that is, "they say". (ما) is negative; (نعبدهم) is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a direct object; (إلا) is a particle of restriction; (ليقربونا): the (لام) is of reason, and (يقربونا) is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied (أن) after the lām of reason; the (واو) is the agent, and (نا) the direct object; (إلى الله) is attached to (يقربونا); and (زلفى) is a maṣdar of confirmation, not of the verb's own maṣdar, but it meets its governor in meaning; the implied form is "so that they bring us near, nearness". Abū al-Baqāʾ allowed it to be parsed as a confirming ḥāl.
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَهُمْ فِي ما هُمْ فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ) (إن) and its subject; the clause (يحكم) is its khabar. Some allowed that His words «إن الله يحكم بينهم» be the khabar of (الذين), in which case the place of the implied saying is accusative as a ḥāl, that is, "saying that". (بينهم) is an adverb attached to (يحكم); (فيما) is also attached to (يحكم); (هم) is mubtadaʾ; (فيه) is attached to (يختلفون); the clause (يختلفون) is their khabar; and the nominal sentence is the ṣila of (ما).
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ لا يَهْدِي مَنْ هُوَ كاذِبٌ كَفَّارٌ) (إن) and its subject; the clause (لا يهدي) is its khabar; the agent of (يهدي) is a latent pronoun referring to Allah; (من) is a direct object; (هو) is mubtadaʾ; (كاذب كفار) are two khabars of it; and the nominal sentence is the ṣila of (من).

* Benefits:
The particles of alerting: «ها», «ألا» and «أما». The difference between «أما» and «ألا» is that «أما» is for the present or the past, and «ألا» for the future. You say:
«أما إن زيدا عاقل» (Indeed, Zayd is intelligent), meaning he is intelligent at present, and you do not say «ألا»; and you say «ألا إن زيدا لا يخاف» (Indeed, Zayd will not fear), that is, in the future, and you do not say «أما». The difference between the two of them and «ها» is that they enter only at the beginning of speech, before a sentence, whereas «ها» enters before the pronoun and the demonstratives even when not at the beginning of speech. «أما» enters before an oath, and «ألا» often before the vocative.
Once this is established: is (ألا) here for the future, although the religion belonging to Allah holds at every time? The answer is that the future is meant here with respect to those who embrace the pure religion; moreover, the two may alternate, that is, «ألا» may come merely as an opener, with no alerting intended.

dervis-irab:67-75.t:
* I'rab:
(وَما قَدَرُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ): a resumptive discourse, introduced to depict His power, the Exalted. ما is negative; قدروا الله is a verb, agent and direct object — that is, they did not know His true nature and did not know Him as He truly deserves to be known. حق قدره is accusative as mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object).
(وَالْأَرْضُ جَمِيعاً قَبْضَتُهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ وَالسَّماواتُ مَطْوِيَّاتٌ بِيَمِينِهِ): the و is the wāw of ḥāl (circumstantial); الأرض is the mubtadaʾ (subject), جميعا is a ḥāl, and قبضته is its khabar (predicate); the clause is a ḥāl of الله. يوم القيامة is an adverbial attached to an omitted ḥāl of قبضته, or else it is attached to قبضته itself, by understanding it to carry the sense of "seized" (مقبوضة). السموات is a mubtadaʾ and مطويات its khabar, and بيمينه are two [elements: preposition and genitive] attached to مطويات. The wording of Abū l-Baqāʾ: «الأرض is a mubtadaʾ and قبضته the khabar, and جميعا is a ḥāl of الأرض; the implied form is: when it is gathered together, it is His grasp, that is, seized. So the operator in إذا is the maṣdar (verbal noun), because it has the meaning of a passive participle. Abū ʿAlī stated in al-Ḥujja that the implied form is "ذات قبضته" (the holder of His grasp), but this was rejected, on the ground that a muḍāf ilayhi does not govern what precedes it; yet this is not sound, because it is now no longer a muḍāf ilayhi, and once the muḍāf is omitted its ruling does not remain. قبضته is also read in the accusative, in the sense of "in His grasp", but this is weak, because this adverbial is a delimited one, so it is like your saying "Zayd [is] the house". السموات مطويات is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, and بيمينه are two [elements] attached to the khabar; it may also be a ḥāl from the pronoun in the khabar, or a second khabar. مطويات is also read with the kasra [i.e. in the accusative, as a ḥāl], with بيمينه as the khabar. It is also said that the khabar is omitted, that is: "and the heavens are His grasp".» Further discussion of this verse will come in the section on rhetoric.
(سُبْحانَهُ وَتَعالى عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ): سبحانه is a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb; تعالى is a past verb whose agent is a latent pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted; عما are two [elements] attached to تعالى; and the clause يشركون is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما. (وَنُفِخَ فِي الصُّورِ فَصَعِقَ مَنْ فِي السَّماواتِ وَمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ إِلَّا مَنْ شاءَ اللَّهُ): the و is a conjunction linking to what preceded; what is to come is expressed in the past tense because its occurrence is certain. نفخ is a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he", referring to the blower — it is said that he is Isrāfīl, or Isrāfīl and Jibrīl. في الصور are two [elements] attached to نفخ. فصعق is conjoined to نفخ; من is the fāʿil, and في السموات and من في الأرض are the ṣila of من. إلا is a particle of exception and من is the excepted. There is disagreement about who the excepted are, with many opinions, to be found in the longer works. The clause شاء الله is the ṣila of من. (ثُمَّ نُفِخَ فِيهِ أُخْرى فَإِذا هُمْ قِيامٌ يَنْظُرُونَ): ثم is a conjunction of sequence with delay, owing to the interval between the two blasts. نفخ is a passive past verb, فيه are two [elements] attached to نفخ, and أخرى is the deputy agent of نفخ, as in His saying, the Exalted, «فإذا نفخ في الصور نفخة واحدة». It is also permissible that the preposition and its genitive noun stand in the place of the deputy agent, with أخرى an adjective of an omitted maṣdar that it replaces, that is, it is a mafʿūl muṭlaq. The فاء is a conjunction, and إذا is the إذا of surprise, with no grammatical position; هم is the mubtadaʾ and قيام the khabar; the clause ينظرون is a second khabar. The meaning of ينظرون is that they turn their eyes in all directions, like the gaze of one who is stunned and bewildered when a calamity strikes him suddenly.
(وَأَشْرَقَتِ الْأَرْضُ بِنُورِ رَبِّها وَوُضِعَ الْكِتابُ): the و is a conjunction; أشرقت الأرض is a verb and agent; بنور ربها are two [elements] attached to أشرقت. ووضع الكتاب is conjoined to what precedes; وضع is a passive past verb and الكتاب the deputy agent. The ال in الكتاب is generic, that is, each one is given his book, meaning the scrolls of his deeds in which his good deeds or evil deeds are recorded. (وَجِيءَ بِالنَّبِيِّينَ وَالشُّهَداءِ وَقُضِيَ بَيْنَهُمْ بِالْحَقِّ وَهُمْ لا يُظْلَمُونَ): وجيء is likewise conjoined to what precedes; بالنبيين are two [elements] attached to جيء, and الشهداء is conjoined to النبيين. قضي is a passive past verb; بينهم either takes the place of the deputy agent, or is attached to قضي with the deputy agent omitted, implied from the maṣdar understood from the verb, that is, "judgment was passed". بالحق are two [elements] attached to an omitted ḥāl. The و is the wāw of ḥāl; هم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause لا يظلمون is the khabar; the clause is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl.
(وَوُفِّيَتْ كُلُّ نَفْسٍ ما عَمِلَتْ وَهُوَ أَعْلَمُ بِما يَفْعَلُونَ): ووفيت is likewise conjoined; كل نفس is the deputy agent; ما is the second direct object of وفيت, and the clause عملت is its ṣila. You may also take ما as maṣdarī, i.e. "its doing", in which case the interpreted maṣdar is the second object. The و is circumstantial or conjunctive; هو is a mubtadaʾ and أعلم the khabar; بما are two [elements] attached to أعلم; and the clause يفعلون is a ṣila. (وَسِيقَ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا إِلى جَهَنَّمَ زُمَراً): the و is a conjunction; سيق is a passive past verb and الذين the deputy agent; the clause كفروا is a ṣila; إلى جهنم are two [elements] attached to سيق; and زمرا is a ḥāl. It is the plural of زمرة, and the زمرة is a group. Its derivation is from الزمر, which is sound, because a group always has a sound. One says زمر يزمر (from the two patterns "dakhala" and "ḍaraba"), meaning "he sang by blowing into a reed and the like". (حَتَّى إِذا جاؤُها فُتِحَتْ أَبْوابُها): حتى is inceptive (ibtidāʾiyya) — the discussion of حتى has already been given at length. إذا is an adverb of future time containing the meaning of a condition; the clause جاءوها is in the position of genitive by the adverb's annexation to it; and the clause فتحت أبوابها has no grammatical position, because it is the apodosis of إذا; أبوابها is the deputy agent.
(وَقالَ لَهُمْ خَزَنَتُها أَلَمْ يَأْتِكُمْ رُسُلٌ مِنْكُمْ يَتْلُونَ عَلَيْكُمْ آياتِ رَبِّكُمْ): وقال is conjoined to فتحت; لهم are two [elements] attached to قال; خزنتها is the agent of قال; the hamza is for interrogation of affirmation and rebuke; لم is a particle of negation, inversion (of tense) and jussive; يأت is an imperfect verb jussive by لم; the ك is a direct object; رسل is the agent; منكم is an adjective of رسل; the clause يتلون is a second adjective, or a ḥāl; عليكم are two [elements] attached to يتلون; and آيات ربكم is the object of يتلون. (وَيُنْذِرُونَكُمْ لِقاءَ يَوْمِكُمْ هذا): وينذرونكم is conjoined to يتلون; لقاء يومكم is a second direct object, or accusative by removal of the preposition; يومكم is annexed to لقاء, and by it is meant the time of their entering the Fire. The use of "day" and "days" has become common for times of hardship. هذا is an adjective of يومكم or a badal from it. (قالُوا بَلى وَلكِنْ حَقَّتْ كَلِمَةُ الْعَذابِ عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ): بلى is a particle of response, to affirm a negation, that is: "Yes, they came to us and recited to us". The و is a conjunction; لكن is a particle of rectification, inoperative; حقت كلمة العذاب is a verb and agent; and على الكافرين are two [elements] attached to حقت.
(قِيلَ ادْخُلُوا أَبْوابَ جَهَنَّمَ خالِدِينَ فِيها فَبِئْسَ مَثْوَى الْمُتَكَبِّرِينَ): a resumptive clause; the clause ادخلوا is the content of what was said; أبواب جهنم is a direct object by extension (ʿalā l-siʿa); خالدين is a ḥāl; فيها are two [elements] attached to خالدين; the فاء is resumptive; بئس is an invariable past verb for the expression of censure; مثوى المتكبرين is its agent; and the one specified for censure is omitted, that is, "it" (هي). (وَسِيقَ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا رَبَّهُمْ إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ زُمَراً): its i'rab has been given verbatim above, and the difference between the two drivings will come in the section on rhetoric.
(حَتَّى إِذا جاؤُها وَفُتِحَتْ أَبْوابُها): حتى is inceptive, and إذا is an adverb of future time containing the meaning of a condition; the clause جاءوها is in the position of genitive by the adverb's annexation to it. Its apodosis here is omitted, because it concerns the description of the people of Paradise, so its omission indicates something that cannot be fathomed and that description cannot encompass. The و is a conjunction, and the clause وفتحت أبوابها is conjoined to جاءوها; more will be said about it later.
(وَقالَ لَهُمْ خَزَنَتُها سَلامٌ عَلَيْكُمْ طِبْتُمْ فَادْخُلُوها خالِدِينَ): the و is a conjunction; وقال لهم خزنتها is a verb and agent; سلام is a mubtadaʾ and عليكم its khabar; طبتم is a verb and agent. فادخلوها: the فاء is causal; ادخلوها is a verb, agent and object; خالدين is a ḥāl. (وَقالُوا الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي صَدَقَنا وَعْدَهُ): a discourse conjoined to the omitted apodosis of إذا, that is, "they entered it and said". الحمد is a mubtadaʾ and لله its khabar, and the clause is the content of what was said; الذي is an adjective, and the clause صدقنا is a ṣila — a past verb, a latent agent, a first direct object, and وعده a second direct object. (وَأَوْرَثَنَا الْأَرْضَ نَتَبَوَّأُ مِنَ الْجَنَّةِ حَيْثُ نَشاءُ فَنِعْمَ أَجْرُ الْعامِلِينَ): the clause وأورثنا is conjoined to صدقنا; الأرض is a second direct object; the clause نتبوأ is a ḥāl from the object of أورثنا, its agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "we"; من الجنة are two [elements] attached to an omitted ḥāl; and حيث is a locative in its normal usage, attached to نتبوأ, or it is the object of نتبوأ. Al-Zamakhsharī said:
«Each one of them will have a garden whose vastness cannot be described and which exceeds his need; so he settles in his garden wherever he wishes and has no need of anyone else's garden.» The فاء is resumptive, and نعم أجر العاملين has had its i'rab given earlier.
(وَتَرَى الْمَلائِكَةَ حَافِّينَ مِنْ حَوْلِ الْعَرْشِ يُسَبِّحُونَ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّهِمْ): a resumptive discourse, introduced to describe the angels brought near on that day. وترى الملائكة is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a direct object; حافين is a ḥāl, that is, surrounding and encircling the Throne, ranged along its edge and sides; من حول العرش are two [elements] attached to حافين; and the clause يسبحون بحمد ربهم is a second ḥāl. (وَقُضِيَ بَيْنَهُمْ بِالْحَقِّ وَقِيلَ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعالَمِينَ): the و is a conjunction; قضي is a passive verb; بينهم is an adverbial standing in for the agent of the agent [sic], or attached to قضي, with the deputy agent a maṣdar understood from the verb, that is, "judgment was passed". [Translator's note: the source says «نائب عن فاعل الفاعل», literally "standing in for the agent of the agent"; translated as written.] بالحق is a ḥāl. The pronoun in بينهم refers to the servants and the angels together. It is also said that [وقيل] is conjoined to قضي, and the clause الحمد لله رب العالمين is the content of what was said.

* Rhetoric:
The close of Sūrat al-Zumar is distinguished by its mention of the states of the Resurrection, praise and glorification, as it is distinguished by sublimity (jazāla) of expression. By sublimity we do not mean that the wording should be strange and rugged, with the roughness of the desert; rather we mean that the wording should be solid and strong while being sweet in the mouth and pleasing in sound to the ear. If we look at the thunderous warnings of the Qur'an where reckoning, punishment, the Scale and the Bridge are mentioned, and where death and the departure from this world and the like are mentioned, we find nothing in them of strange wording, nor anything rugged, plunging into coarseness and harshness. We shall now proceed to explain the figures that occur in it.
1- Metaphor (majāz):
The first of these is the majāz in His saying «والأرض جميعا قبضته يوم القيامة والسموات مطويات بيمينه», for Allah's seizing of the earth is an expression of His power and His encompassing of all His creatures. One says: "So-and-so is in my grasp", meaning that he is in my power, considering what it comes to, because the one who seizes does with what he seizes as he wishes. The قبضة is the single instance of seizing. By "the earth" is meant the seven earths, to which two witnesses attest: the first is His saying جميعا and the second His saying السموات. The folding of the heavens and the earth is also majāz; He does not mean folding as we understand it, but rather passing away and annihilation. And اليمين in the speech of the Arabs comes in the sense of power and dominion, as we have said before.
2- The difference between the two drivings:
In His saying «وسيق», with respect to the people of the Fire and the people of Paradise — in that He expressed the going of both groups with a single word — is a subtle art, which is that the speaker brings a single word that at one time indicates humiliation and punishment, and then brings it a second time to indicate honour and good reward. How beautiful is al-Zamakhsharī's saying on this point. He said: «If you ask: how did He express the going of both groups with the word "driving"? I say: what is meant by the driving of the people of the Fire is their being repelled toward it with humiliation and violence, as is done to captives and those who rebel against the sultan when they are driven to prison or to execution; and what is meant by the driving of the people of Paradise is the driving of their mounts, for they are taken only riding, and urging them on to hasten to the abode of honour and good pleasure, as is done to one who is elevated and honoured among those arriving at the court of some king. How great is the difference between the two drivings!»

* Benefits:
1- The opinions of the grammarians on the apodosis of إذا:
The grammarians have expounded at length on the apodosis of إذا and the secret of the coming of the wāw in His saying «حتى إذا جاءوها وفتحت أبوابها». We have set out in the section on i'rab what we prefer. As for al-Samīn, he summarised the opinions of the grammarians in his saying: «There are three views on the apodosis of إذا. The first is His saying وفتحت, with the wāw redundant (zāʾida); this is the opinion of the Kufans and al-Akhfash. The wāw was brought here, and not in the earlier one, because the doors of prisons are closed until the offender arrives, whereupon they are opened for him and then closed on him, so the absence of the wāw suited them; unlike the doors of joy and gladness, which are opened in anticipation of whoever will enter them. The second is that the apodosis is omitted. Al-Zamakhsharī said that it is proper to imply it after خالدين, that is, because what is conjoined to it does not come after the elements dependent on the condition; and the implied form is: "they were reassured". Al-Mubarrad implied it as: "they were made happy". On these two views the clause وفتحت أبوابها is in the position of accusative as a ḥāl. Some called this wāw the "wāw of eight", saying that the doors of Paradise are eight; and likewise they said about His saying, the Exalted: وثامنهم كلبهم. It is also said that its implied form is: "until when they came to it, they came to it, and its doors were opened" — that is, the apodosis is in the wording of the protasis, but it adds to it by restricting it with the ḥāl, and so it is sound.»
2- An enjoyable chapter by al-Rummānī:
We now quote a full summary of the chapter that ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā al-Rummānī wrote in his great tafsīr, which is lost. How we regret that this book has been lost between the hearing of the earth and its sight! But what consoles us is that al-Suyūṭī quoted much from it, and everyone who wrote on the author's biography mentioned it. Al-Rummānī was a grammarian and theologian, the master of Arabic in his time, devoted to logic so that it came to dominate all his writings and speech. Al-Ṣāḥib was asked: "Why did you not compose a tafsīr?" He said:
"Has ʿAlī ibn ʿĪsā left us anything?" And al-Rummānī himself used to say:
«My tafsīr is an orchard from which you pick whatever you desire.» His tafsīr became well known among people and was frequently mentioned in their books, but it has not reached us. In his study of the secret of beauty in the Qur'an, when discussing this verse, he says: «It is as if it were said: they obtained lasting bliss untroubled by any vexation or disturbance. Omission in a case like this is more eloquent than mention, because the soul goes in every direction in it, whereas if the apodosis were mentioned it would fall short of the aspect that the exposition contains.
[Translator's note: the source text ends here, with the opening quotation mark never closed.]

dervis-irab:33-38.t:
* I'rab:
(وَالَّذِي جاءَ بِالصِّدْقِ وَصَدَّقَ بِهِ أُولئِكَ هُمُ الْمُتَّقُونَ) The wāw is resumptive; الذي is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause جاء بالصدق is the ṣila (relative clause); وصدق is conjoined to the ṣila. الذي is a generic term: what is meant by it in relation to the first ṣila is Muḥammad, and in relation to the second ṣila the believers; therefore the sense of الذي was observed in «أولئك هم المتقون». أولئك is a mubtadaʾ, هم is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl), المتقون is the khabar (predicate) of أولئك, and the nominal clause is the khabar of الذي. This meaning is supported by the reading of Ibn Masʿūd: «والذين جاءوا بالصدق وصدقوا به». (لَهُمْ ما يَشاؤُنَ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِمْ ذلِكَ جَزاءُ الْمُحْسِنِينَ) لهم is a fronted khabar; ما is a postponed mubtadaʾ; the clause يشاءون is its ṣila; عند ربهم is an adverbial attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause is a second khabar of الذي; ذلك is a mubtadaʾ and جزاء المحسنين its khabar, and the clause is accusative as a ḥāl. (لِيُكَفِّرَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ أَسْوَأَ الَّذِي عَمِلُوا) The lām is for causation; يكفر is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied أنْ after the lām of causation; the lām of causation and its genitive noun are attached to an omitted element, i.e. "that was made easy for them so that He may expiate". You may also attach the lām and what follows it to المحسنين, in which case it is the lām of consequence ("so their outcome was expiation"). الله is the agent of يكفر; عنهم is attached to يكفر; أسوأ is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); الذي is a muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); the clause عملوا is the ṣila. The elative here does not carry its proper comparative sense; rather it is the annexation of a thing to its own class without comparison, as in their saying "al-Ashajj and al-Nāqiṣ are the most just of the Banū Marwān", because if the elative were in its proper sense, the construction of the speech would imply that He expiates only the vilest of their evil deeds, and that is naturally not intended.
(وَيَجْزِيَهُمْ أَجْرَهُمْ بِأَحْسَنِ الَّذِي كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ) Conjoined to what precedes; أجرهم is a second direct object of يجزيهم; and what was said about the meaning of the elative أسوأ is said here about the elative أحسن, because He the Exalted does not reward them only for the best of their good deeds. (أَلَيْسَ اللَّهُ بِكافٍ عَبْدَهُ) The hamza is for affirmative interrogation (istifhām taqrīrī), because the hamza of denial, when it enters a negation, affirms it by way of emphasis; ليس with its noun; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition; كاف is genitive in form and accusative in position as the khabar of ليس; عبده is the direct object of كاف. What is meant by it is the Prophet, or the class in general, and this is supported by the reading of Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī: عباده.
(وَيُخَوِّفُونَكَ بِالَّذِينَ مِنْ دُونِهِ وَمَنْ يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ فَما لَهُ مِنْ هادٍ) You may make the wāw circumstantial, so that the clause is a ḥāl, the meaning being "Is Allah not sufficient for you while they try to frighten you?" This is if by "servant" He meant His Prophet ﷺ. Or you may make it resumptive, so that the clause is resumptive, brought to refute what they do in frightening [him] with the idols. يخوفونك is an imperfect verb with a direct object; بالذين is attached to يخوفونك; من دونه is attached to an omitted element which is the ṣila. As for «ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد», its i'rab was given verbatim a little earlier, so renew your acquaintance with it. (وَمَنْ يَهْدِ اللَّهُ فَما لَهُ مِنْ مُضِلٍّ أَلَيْسَ اللَّهُ بِعَزِيزٍ ذِي انْتِقامٍ) The clause is conjoined to the preceding clause and the i'rab is similar. The hamza is for affirmative interrogation; ليس with its noun; the bāʾ in بعزيز is a redundant preposition and عزيز is genitive in form and accusative in position as the khabar of ليس; ذي انتقام is an adjective (naʿt).
(وَلَئِنْ سَأَلْتَهُمْ مَنْ خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ لَيَقُولُنَّ اللَّهُ) The wāw is a conjunction and the lām prepares for an oath (lām muwaṭṭiʾa); إن is conditional; سألتهم is a verb, agent and direct object, and it is in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); مَن is an interrogative noun in the position of the nominative, a mubtadaʾ, and the clause خلق السموات والأرض is its khabar, and the clause is in the position of the accusative as the second direct object of سألتهم, whose operation is suspended by the interrogative; the lām falls in the answer to the oath, and the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted according to the well-known rule; يقولن is an imperfect verb that is declinable (muʿrab) because the emphatic nūn does not directly attach to it, and many parallels of it have preceded; الله is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "He is Allah", or a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted, i.e. "created them". (قُلْ أَفَرَأَيْتُمْ ما تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ) The hamza is interrogative and the fāʾ is the fāʾ faṣīḥa (the eloquent fāʾ); رأيتم means "tell me", and this has been discussed in detail more than once; ما تدعون is the first direct object of رأيتم; من دون الله is a ḥāl. It is also possible for the fāʾ to be conjoined to an implied element, i.e. "Have you reflected after what you have acknowledged, and so have you considered…". (إِنْ أَرادَنِيَ اللَّهُ بِضُرٍّ هَلْ هُنَّ كاشِفاتُ ضُرِّهِ) إن is conditional; أرادني الله is a verb with a fronted direct object and a postponed agent, and it is in the position of the jussive as the protasis; the apodosis is omitted; the conditional clause is parenthetical; the interrogative clause هل هن كاشفات is the second direct object of رأيتم; هن is a mubtadaʾ and كاشفات ضره its khabar.
(أَوْ أَرادَنِي بِرَحْمَةٍ هَلْ هُنَّ مُمْسِكاتُ رَحْمَتِهِ) Conjoined to the preceding clause. It was also read with tanwīn on كاشفات and ممسكات and with the accusative ضره and رحمته, as direct objects of the two active participles. (قُلْ حَسْبِيَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ يَتَوَكَّلُ الْمُتَوَكِّلُونَ) حسبي الله is a mubtadaʾ and khabar, or the reverse, and the clause is the content of the saying; عليه is attached to يتوكل; يتوكل المتوكلون is an imperfect verb and agent.

dervis-irab:39-42.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ يا قَوْمِ اعْمَلُوا عَلى مَكانَتِكُمْ إِنِّي عامِلٌ فَسَوْفَ تَعْلَمُونَ) يا is a vocative particle; قوم is the one addressed (munādā), annexed to the omitted first-person yāʾ; اعملوا is an imperative verb and agent; على مكانتكم is a ḥāl (circumstantial), and the meaning of the metaphor here will come in the section on Rhetoric; inna with its noun and khabar, and in the speech there is an omission, i.e. "according to my position"; the fāʾ is a conjunction; سوف is a particle of futurity; تعلمون is an imperfect nominative verb, and the wāw is the agent. (مَنْ يَأْتِيهِ عَذابٌ يُخْزِيهِ وَيَحِلُّ عَلَيْهِ عَذابٌ مُقِيمٌ) مَن is a relative noun, the direct object of تعلمون, and knowing here means acquaintance, so it takes one object; the clause يأتيه is the ṣila (relative clause); عذاب is the agent of يأتيه; the clause يخزيه is an adjective of عذاب; ويحل is conjoined to يخزيه; عليه is attached to يحل; عذاب is the agent of يحل; مقيم is an adjective, i.e. permanent and fixed. (إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنا عَلَيْكَ الْكِتابَ لِلنَّاسِ بِالْحَقِّ) inna with its noun, and the clause أنزلنا is its khabar; عليك is attached to أنزلنا; الكتاب is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); للناس is attached to أنزلنا, i.e. for their sake; بالحق is a ḥāl, i.e. "accompanied by it", so it is from the agent or from the object. (فَمَنِ اهْتَدى فَلِنَفْسِهِ وَمَنْ ضَلَّ فَإِنَّما يَضِلُّ عَلَيْها) The fāʾ is a conjunction; مَن is a conditional noun that jusses, in the position of the nominative, a mubtadaʾ; اهتدى is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the fāʾ is the connecting fāʾ; لنفسه is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "his guidance is for himself", and the clause is in the position of the jussive as the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ); the protasis and its apodosis are the khabar of the mubtadaʾ. The clause «ومن ضل فإنما يضل عليها» is conjoined to its counterpart.
(وَما أَنْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ بِوَكِيلٍ) The wāw is a conjunction; ما is the negative Ḥijāzī mā; أنت is its noun; عليهم is attached to وكيل; the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition and وكيل is genitive in form and accusative in position as the khabar of ما. (اللَّهُ يَتَوَفَّى الْأَنْفُسَ حِينَ مَوْتِها وَالَّتِي لَمْ تَمُتْ فِي مَنامِها) الله is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يتوفى الأنفس its khabar; حين موتها is attached to يتوفى; the wāw is a conjunction; التي is conjoined to الأنفس; the clause لم تمت في منامها is the ṣila; and في منامها is an adverbial of يتوفى. The meaning is: "and He takes the souls that have not died, in their sleep", i.e. He takes them when they sleep, and of this is His saying the Exalted: «وهو الذي يتوفاكم بالليل». (فَيُمْسِكُ الَّتِي قَضى عَلَيْهَا الْمَوْتَ وَيُرْسِلُ الْأُخْرى إِلى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى) The fāʾ is a conjunction; يمسك is an imperfect verb conjoined to يتوفى; التي is the direct object of يمسك; the clause قضى عليها الموت is the ṣila; الموت is the direct object of قضى; ويرسل is conjoined to يمسك; الأخرى is a direct object; إلى أجل is attached to يرسل or to يمسك; مسمى is an adjective of أجل.
(إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآياتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ) إنّ is a particle resembling the verb; في ذلك is a fronted khabar; the lām is the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); آيات is the noun of إنّ; لقوم is an adjective of آيات; the clause يتفكرون is an adjective (naʿt) of قوم.

* Rhetoric:
In His saying «قل يا قوم اعملوا على مكانتكم» to the end of the verse is an istiʿāra taṣrīḥiyya (explicit metaphor): the state is likened to the place in which one is settled, the point of likeness being their steadfastness in that state, like the steadfastness of one established in his place.

dervis-irab:4-6.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يُكَوِّرُ): takwīr is wrapping and winding. One says "he wound (kāra) the turban on his head" and "he coiled it (kawwarahā)". There are several aspects to it, as al-Zamakhsharī says:
1- Night and day follow one another: this one departs and that one covers its place, as though he clothed it and wrapped it, as a garment is wrapped around the wearer. From this is the saying of Dhū al-Rumma describing the mirage:
تلوى الثنايا بحقويها حواشيه ... لي الملاء بأبواب التفاريج
(Its edges are twisted around its waist at the mountain passes, as shawls are wound at the doors of the tafārīj.)
Al-thanāyā are the mountain passes; al-ḥaqw is the waist; al-ḥawāshī are the sides; al-malāʾ is the plural of mulāʾa, which is the cloak; and al-tafārīj is the plural of tafrāj, which is the small door and the garment of brocade. He ascribed the winding to the passes because they are the cause of the twisting. He likened the encompassing of its sides and its piling up at the sides of the pass to the winding of a cloak at the doors of the tafārīj.
2- Each of them hides the other when it comes upon it, so its hiding of it was likened to something visible which wraps around that which it hides, removing it from the reach of sight.
3- This one returns upon that one in continuous succession, so this was likened to the succession of the coils of a turban, one upon the track of another.

* I'rab:
(لَوْ أَرادَ اللَّهُ أَنْ يَتَّخِذَ وَلَداً لَاصْطَفى مِمَّا يَخْلُقُ ما يَشاءُ) (لو) is a non-jussive conditional particle; (أراد) is a past verb; (الله) is the agent; (أن) and what is within its scope is the object of (أراد). The (لام) links the answer of (لو); (اصطفى) is a past verb whose agent is "he", that is, Allah the Exalted, and the clause has no grammatical position. (مما) is attached to (اصطفى); the clause (يخلق) is the ṣila of (ما); the (ما) is a direct object; the clause (يشاء) is the ṣila of (ما); and the returning pronoun is omitted, that is, "He wills it". (سُبْحانَهُ هُوَ اللَّهُ الْواحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ) (سبحانه) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq of an omitted verb, glorifying Him the Exalted above anyone's being as they ascribed to Him. (هو) is mubtadaʾ; (الله) is its khabar; and (الواحد القهار) are two adjectives of (الله). (خَلَقَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضَ بِالْحَقِّ) (خلق) is a past verb with a latent agent referring to Allah the Exalted; (السموات) is a direct object; (الأرض) is conjoined to (السموات); and (بالحق) is a ḥāl. (يُكَوِّرُ اللَّيْلَ عَلَى النَّهارِ وَيُكَوِّرُ النَّهارَ عَلَى اللَّيْلِ) The clause is a ḥāl clause or resumptive, explaining how He disposes of the heavens and the earth. (الليل) is a direct object; (على النهار) is attached to (يكور); and (يكور النهار على الليل) is conjoined to its counterpart.
(وَسَخَّرَ الشَّمْسَ وَالْقَمَرَ كُلٌّ يَجْرِي لِأَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى أَلا هُوَ الْعَزِيزُ الْغَفَّارُ) (وسخر الشمس والقمر) is conjoined to (خلق السموات والأرض). (كل) is mubtadaʾ and the clause (يجري) is the khabar; (لأجل) is attached to (يجري); and (مسمى) is an adjective of (أجل). (ألا) is a particle of alerting which heads the sentence to show the degree of concern for it and attention to its import; (هو) is mubtadaʾ; and (العزيز الغفار) are two khabars of (هو). (خَلَقَكُمْ مِنْ نَفْسٍ واحِدَةٍ ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنْها زَوْجَها) (خلقكم) is a past verb, a latent agent and a direct object; (من نفس) is a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (خلقكم); (واحدة) is an adjective of (نفس), and by it Ādam is meant. (ثم) is a particle of order and delay; the secret of joining with it will come in the section on rhetoric. (جعل) is a past verb whose agent is a latent pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted; (منها) is attached to (جعل) because it means "created"; and (زوجها) is a direct object. (وَأَنْزَلَ لَكُمْ مِنَ الْأَنْعامِ ثَمانِيَةَ أَزْواجٍ) (وأنزل) is conjoined to (خلقكم); (لكم) is attached to an omitted ḥāl; (من الأنعام) is attached to (أنزل); and (ثمانية أزواج) is a direct object. The meaning of the pairs has already been given in Sūrat al-Anʿām.
(يَخْلُقُكُمْ فِي بُطُونِ أُمَّهاتِكُمْ خَلْقاً مِنْ بَعْدِ خَلْقٍ فِي ظُلُماتٍ ثَلاثٍ) The clause is a ḥāl clause or resumptive, explaining how what was mentioned is created. (يخلقكم) is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a direct object; (في بطون أمهاتكم) is attached to (يخلقكم); (خلقا) is a mafʿūl muṭlaq; and (من بعد خلق) is an adjective of it; it may also be attached to (يخلقكم), in which case the maṣdar is merely for emphasis. Al-Bayḍāwī said: «that is, a perfect living being, after bones clothed with flesh, after bare bones, after a morsel of flesh, after a clot, after sperm-drops.» [Translator's note: the closing quotation mark is missing in the source.] (في ظلمات) is attached to the genitive (خلق) which precedes it. It may not be attached to the accusative (خلقا) because that is a confirming maṣdar and so does not govern, nor to (يخلق) because a preposition like it is already attached to it, and two particles identical in form and meaning are not attached to the same word except as a substitute or by conjunction. If you make (في ظلمات) a badal of (في بطون أمهاتكم), a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl), because the wombs include them, and it is a substitute with repetition of the governor, that is permissible. What is meant by the three darknesses will come in the section on benefits.
(ذلِكُمُ اللَّهُ رَبُّكُمْ لَهُ الْمُلْكُ لا إِلهَ إِلَّا هُوَ فَأَنَّى تُصْرَفُونَ) (ذلكم) is mubtadaʾ; (الله) is its first khabar; (ربكم) its second khabar; (له) is a fronted khabar; (الملك) is a deferred mubtadaʾ; and the nominal sentence is a third khabar; the clause (لا إله إلا هو) is a fourth khabar. The i'rab of the testimony has been given in detail. (فأنى): the (فاء) is resumptive; (أنى) is an interrogative noun attached to an omitted ḥāl; (تصرفون) is an imperfect passive verb, and the (واو) is the deputy agent.

* Rhetoric:
In His words «ثم جعل منها زوجها» the conjunction is with «ثم», which gives order with delay in existence, yet the apparent matter conflicts with that, because the creation of Ḥawwāʾ from Ādam precedes our creation from him. The scholars of rhetoric and the commentators found this conjunction difficult and answered with answers that we cite, after which we favour the one nearest to being preponderant. Al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you ask: what is the point of His words "then He made from it its mate", and the sense of delay that it gives? I say: they are two signs among the signs He enumerated as proof of His oneness and power: the branching out of this uncountable creation from the single self of Ādam, and the creation of Ḥawwāʾ from his qaṣrayān (the qaṣrayān are the two ribs next to the collarbones). But one of the two He made a continuing custom, while the other has no custom running to it, and no female other than Ḥawwāʾ has been created from the ribs of a man. It was therefore more deserving to be a sign and more apt to draw the hearer's wonder. So He joined it with "then" to the first sign to indicate that it is distinct from it in excellence and merit and is removed from it in what returns to the increase of its being a sign. So it is a delay in rank and degree, not a delay in existence.»
Another said: «The conjoined element is connected with the meaning of "one", so "then" is joined to that and not to "created you"; thus the meaning is "He created you from a single self that was made single by being brought into existence, then it was paired with a mate". So here it is in its proper sense, of delay in existence.»
We see both aspects as sound, and it is correct to take the conjunction in either.
Here Ibn Hishām fell into an error of recitation: he cited this verse in the wording «هو الذي خلقكم من نفس واحدة» etc. He cited it as evidence that some people differed over its meaning, which is order, holding on to it. He said: «The answer concerning the verse has five aspects: (The first) that the conjunction is upon an omitted element, that is, "from a single self which He originated, then made from it its mate". (The second) that the conjunction is upon "one" by interpreting it as a verb, that is, "from a self which was single, that is, alone, then He made from it its mate". (The third) that the offspring were brought out of the back of Ādam, peace be upon him, like tiny particles, and then Ḥawwāʾ was created from his ribs. (The fourth) that since the creation of Ḥawwāʾ from Ādam has no custom like it, "then" was brought to announce its order and delay in wonder and the manifestation of power, not order and delay in time. (The fifth) that "then" is for ordering of reports, not ordering of the ruling, as it is said, "What you did today has reached me, then what you did yesterday is more wonderful", that is, then I tell you that what you did yesterday is more wonderful.» [Translator's note: the closing quotation mark of the Zamakhsharī and Ibn Hishām passages is partly missing or misplaced in the source.]

* Benefits:
By His words «في ظلمات ثلاث» He meant the darkness of the belly, the darkness of the womb (raḥim, with fatḥa on the rāʾ and kasra on the ḥāʾ; while al-riḥm with kasra on the rāʾ and sukūn on the ḥāʾ is feminine and is the place where the foetus is deposited in the womb of the pregnant woman), and the darkness of the placenta (mashīma), which is, as in al-Miṣbāḥ, «on the pattern of karīma; its origin is mafʿila with sukūn on the fāʾ and kasra on the ʿayn, but the kasra was heavy on the yāʾ, so it was moved to the shīn; and it is the membrane of the human child.
Ibn al-Aʿrābī said: that in which the child is held is called al-mashīma, al-kīs and al-ghilāf, and the plural is mashīm with omission of the hāʾ, and mashāyim, like maʿīsha and maʿāyish; and in other than humans it is called al-salā.» [Translator's note: the closing quotation mark is missing in the source; here it is placed at the end.]

dervis-irab:43-46.t:
* I'rab:
(أَمِ اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ شُفَعاءَ) أم is a conjunction meaning بل ("rather"); اتخذوا is a past verb and the wāw is the agent, i.e. Quraysh; من دون الله is the second direct object of اتخذوا and شفعاء the first direct object of اتخذوا. (قُلْ أَوَلَوْ كانُوا لا يَمْلِكُونَ شَيْئاً وَلا يَعْقِلُونَ) The hamza is for a rhetorical denial (istifhām inkārī) and what it governs is omitted, its implied form being "Will they intercede?"; the wāw is circumstantial (ḥāl) and لو is conditional; كان with its noun, and the clause لا يملكون is its predicate, and the clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl; the meaning is "Will they intercede while they own nothing and do not reason?" شيئا is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object) or a mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object), and this has been discussed; ولا يعقلون is conjoined to لا يملكون. The apodosis of لو is omitted, its implied form being "you take them", i.e. "even if they are of this description, do you take them?" (قُلْ لِلَّهِ الشَّفاعَةُ جَمِيعاً لَهُ مُلْكُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ ثُمَّ إِلَيْهِ تُرْجَعُونَ) لله is a fronted khabar (predicate) and الشفاعة a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the lām is for ownership, i.e. it belongs to Him alone, no one owns it except by His granting it; جميعا is a ḥāl; له is a fronted khabar and ملك السموات والأرض a postponed mubtadaʾ; ثم is a conjunction of sequence with delay; إليه is attached to ترجعون.
(وَإِذا ذُكِرَ اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ اشْمَأَزَّتْ قُلُوبُ الَّذِينَ لا يُؤْمِنُونَ بِالْآخِرَةِ) The wāw is a conjunction and إذا is an adverb of the future attached to the apodosis; the clause ذكر الله is in the position of the genitive, being the muḍāf ilayhi of the adverb; الله is the nāʾib fāʾil (deputy agent); وحده is a ḥāl, according to al-Khalīl and Sībawayh it is [accusative] as a maṣdar. The clause اشمأزت قلوب الذين لا يؤمنون بالآخرة has no grammatical position, because it is the answer to إذا. (وَإِذا ذُكِرَ الَّذِينَ مِنْ دُونِهِ إِذا هُمْ يَسْتَبْشِرُونَ) Conjoined to what precedes; من دونه is the ṣila of الذين; إذا is the إذا of surprise (fujāʾiyya), and we have taken it to be a particle, so it needs no governing element; if it is an adverb of time or place, it is governed by what follows it; هم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يستبشرون its khabar, i.e. they rejoice at the time of mention of those besides Him. (قُلِ اللَّهُمَّ فاطِرَ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ عالِمَ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهادَةِ) اللهم is a vocative and the doubled mīm is a replacement for يا; this has been discussed in detail before; فاطر السموات والأرض is an annexed vocative; there are other parsings, which will be discussed in detail in the section on Benefits, as will His saying عالم الغيب والشهادة.
(أَنْتَ تَحْكُمُ بَيْنَ عِبادِكَ فِي ما كانُوا فِيهِ يَخْتَلِفُونَ) أنت is a mubtadaʾ and the clause تحكم its khabar; the adverbial بين عبادك is attached to تحكم, and فيما is also attached to تحكم; كانوا is kāna with its noun, and the clause يختلفون is the predicate of كانوا; فيه is attached to يختلفون; the clause كانوا etc. is the ṣila of ما.

* Benefits:
1- Returning to «اللهم»:
The position of al-Khalīl and Sībawayh is that this noun is not described by an adjective, because with the mīm it has become for them like an interjection, i.e. not firmly established in usage. al-Mubarrad and al-Zajjāj held that it may be described, with an adjective that is nominative in form and accusative in position, and they made فاطر السموات والأرض an adjective of it. Abū Ḥayyān said: The sound view is that of Sībawayh, because nothing like "اللهم الرحيم ارحمنا" has been heard, and the verse and its like admit of being a vocative.
Ibn Hishām said: «He said regarding «قل اللهم فاطر السموات والأرض» that it is on the assumption of يا, and did not make it an adjective by position, because in his view the name of Allah, Glorified and Exalted, when the mīm that replaces the vocative particle is attached to it, resembles interjections, so it cannot be described», meaning that it has become like هلّا, the mīm being like a sound added to the name of Allah while both retain their meanings.
2- Istibshār and ishmiʾzāz:
al-Zamakhsharī said: «الاستبشار is for his heart to fill with joy until the skin of his face spreads out and brightens; and الاشمئزاز is for it to fill with distress until contraction shows in the surface of his face.»

dervis-irab:47-49.t:
* I'rab:
(وَلَوْ أَنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا ما فِي الْأَرْضِ جَمِيعاً وَمِثْلَهُ مَعَهُ لَافْتَدَوْا بِهِ مِنْ سُوءِ الْعَذابِ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ) A resumptive statement, brought to explain one kind of the terror awaiting them and the severe punishment prepared for them.
لو is conditional, and أنّ with what is within its scope is the agent of an omitted verb, according to the preferred view, and this has been explained more than once; للذين is its fronted khabar and ما its postponed noun; في الأرض is the ṣila of ما; جميعا is a ḥāl; مثله is conjoined to ما; معه is an adverbial attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl; the lām falls in the answer to لو; افتدوا is a verb and agent; به is attached to افتدوا; من سوء العذاب is also attached to افتدوا; the adverbial يوم القيامة is a ḥāl from the agent of افتدوا, i.e. while they are in that hard day.
(وَبَدا لَهُمْ مِنَ اللَّهِ ما لَمْ يَكُونُوا يَحْتَسِبُونَ) A statement conjoined to the clause «ولو أن للذين ظلموا» to the end of the verse; بدا is a past verb; لهم is attached to it; من الله is a ḥāl; ما is the agent; the clause لم يكونوا is the ṣila of ما; the clause يحتسبون is the khabar of يكونوا, and the returning pronoun is omitted, i.e. "they reckon on it".
(وَبَدا لَهُمْ سَيِّئاتُ ما كَسَبُوا وَحاقَ بِهِمْ ما كانُوا بِهِ يَسْتَهْزِؤُنَ) Conjoined to what precedes. You may also take the two statements as resumptive, brought to bring out their threat in the strongest form a threat and warning can take; their i'rab is similar to what has preceded.
(فَإِذا مَسَّ الْإِنْسانَ ضُرٌّ دَعانا) The fāʾ is a conjunction, for ordering what follows it, as a contradiction, after what was mentioned before; the secret of preferring the fāʾ will come, although at the beginning of the sūra it was conjoined with the wāw; إذا is an adverb of the future containing the meaning of condition; مس الإنسان ضر is a past verb with a fronted direct object and a postponed agent; the clause دعانا has no grammatical position because it is the answer to إذا. (ثُمَّ إِذا خَوَّلْناهُ نِعْمَةً مِنَّا قالَ: إِنَّما أُوتِيتُهُ عَلى عِلْمٍ) ثم is a conjunction of sequence with delay; إذا is an adverb of the future containing the meaning of condition; the clause خولناه is in the position of the genitive, being the muḍāf ilayhi of the adverb; خولناه is a verb, agent and direct object; نعمة is a second direct object; منّا is an adjective of نعمة; the clause قال has no position; إنما is kāffa and makfūfa (inna restricted by mā); أوتيته is a passive past verb, the tāʾ is the deputy agent and the hāʾ is the direct object. The pronoun was made masculine because النعمة carries the meaning of benefaction and gift. You may also let inna operate, making mā a relative noun in the position of the accusative, its noun, with على علم its khabar, but the first is preferable. على علم is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl, i.e. "knowing that I shall be given it, because of the worthiness and entitlement I possess".
(بَلْ هِيَ فِتْنَةٌ وَلكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لا يَعْلَمُونَ) بل is a transitional iḍrāb; هي is a mubtadaʾ and فتنة a khabar, i.e. their aforementioned saying, or the blessing, and this is preferable; ولكن: the wāw is circumstantial; lākinna with its noun, and the clause لا يعلمون is its khabar. al-Farrāʾ said: The pronoun in His saying هي was made feminine because فتنة is feminine, and had He said «بل هو فتنة» it would have been permissible; and the masculine in the first, in أوتيته, is with regard to its meaning.

* Rhetoric:
The saying «فإذا مس الإنسان ضر» was conjoined with the fāʾ at the end of the sūra and with the wāw at its beginning because this one arose out of His saying «وإذا ذكر الله وحده اشمأزت قلوبهم», that is, they shrink from the mention of Allah and rejoice at the mention of the gods.
As for the first, it did not arise out of what precedes it; it is a description of speech that required its conjunction with the wāw, because of its suitability to what precedes.

dervis-irab:50-52.t:
* I'rab:
(قَدْ قالَهَا الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ) قد is a particle of affirmation; قالها is a past verb with a fronted direct object, and the hāʾ refers back to their saying, namely «إنما أوتيته على علم», since it is a "word"; الذين is its agent; من قبلهم is attached to an omitted element which is the ṣila of the relative.
(فَما أَغْنى عَنْهُمْ ما كانُوا يَكْسِبُونَ) The fāʾ is a conjunction; ما is negative; أغنى is a past verb; عنهم is attached to it; ما is the agent of أغنى; the clause كانوا is the ṣila; kāna with its noun, and the clause يكسبون is its khabar. (فَأَصابَهُمْ سَيِّئاتُ ما كَسَبُوا) The fāʾ is a conjunction; أصابهم سيئات is a verb with a fronted direct object and a postponed agent; ما is a relative or a maṣdar particle in the position of the genitive by annexation. (وَالَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا مِنْ هؤُلاءِ سَيُصِيبُهُمْ سَيِّئاتُ ما كَسَبُوا وَما هُمْ بِمُعْجِزِينَ) The wāw is a conjunction; الذين is a mubtadaʾ (subject); the clause ظلموا is the ṣila; من هؤلاء is a ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause سيصيبهم سيئات ما كسبوا is the khabar (predicate) of الذين. وما هم: ما is the negative Ḥijāzī mā, هم its noun, the bāʾ is a redundant (zāʾida) preposition, and معجزين is genitive by the bāʾ in form and accusative in position as the khabar of ما.
(أَوَلَمْ يَعْلَمُوا أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَبْسُطُ الرِّزْقَ لِمَنْ يَشاءُ وَيَقْدِرُ) The hamza is for a rhetorical denial and the wāw is conjoined to an omitted element, its implied form being "Did they say it, and did they not know?"; لم is a particle of negation, reversal and jussive; يعلموا is an imperfect verb jussive by لم, its sign of jussive being the omission of the nūn, and the wāw is the agent; أنّ with what is within its scope fills the place of the two objects of يعلموا; inna with its noun, and the clause يبسط الرزق is its khabar; لمن is attached to يبسط; the clause يشاء is the ṣila; ويقدر is conjoined to يبسط.
(إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَآياتٍ لِقَوْمٍ يُؤْمِنُونَ) inna and its fronted khabar; the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); آيات is its postponed noun; لقوم is an adjective of آيات, and the clause يؤمنون is an adjective of قوم.

dervis-irab:7-8.t:
* I'rab:
(إِنْ تَكْفُرُوا فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ غَنِيٌّ عَنْكُمْ وَلا يَرْضى لِعِبادِهِ الْكُفْرَ وَإِنْ تَشْكُرُوا يَرْضَهُ لَكُمْ) (إن) is a jussive conditional particle; (تكفروا) is the protasis, its sign of jussive being the omission of the nūn, and the (واو) is the agent. The (فاء) is a linking particle; (إن) with its subject and khabar, and the clause is the apodosis; (عنكم) is attached to (غني). (وإن تشكروا) is conjoined to (إن تكفروا). (يرضه) is the apodosis, its sign of jussive being the omission of the weak letter, and the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "He", referring to Allah the Exalted; the (هاء) is an attached pronoun in the position of the accusative as direct object, read with ḍamma, with sukūn, with lengthening and without it. (وَلا تَزِرُ وازِرَةٌ وِزْرَ أُخْرى ثُمَّ إِلى رَبِّكُمْ مَرْجِعُكُمْ فَيُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِما كُنْتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ) The (واو) is a conjunction; (لا) is negative; (تزر) is an imperfect nominative verb; (وازرة) is the agent; (وزر) is a direct object, that is, "no soul bears the burden of another soul"; and (أخرى) is a muḍāf ilayhi with an omitted qualified noun, that is, "another soul". (ثم) is a conjunction of delay; (إلى ربكم) is a fronted khabar; (مرجعكم) is a deferred mubtadaʾ; the (فاء) is a conjunction; (ينبئكم) is an imperfect verb, a latent agent and a direct object; (بما) is attached to (ينبئكم); (كنتم): (كان) and its subject; the clause (تعملون) is its khabar; and the clause (كنتم تعملون) is the ṣila of the relative. (إِنَّهُ عَلِيمٌ بِذاتِ الصُّدُورِ) (إن) with its subject and khabar; (بذات الصدور) is attached to (عليم); and the sentence gives the reason for the informing about deeds.
(وَإِذا مَسَّ الْإِنْسانَ ضُرٌّ دَعا رَبَّهُ مُنِيباً إِلَيْهِ) The (واو) is resumptive; (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the meaning of a condition; (مس) is a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa; (الإنسان) is a fronted direct object; (ضر) is a deferred mubtadaʾ; and by harm all that is disliked is meant. The clause (دعا) has no grammatical position, because it is the answer to a non-jussive condition; (ربه) is a direct object; (منيبا) is a ḥāl; and (إليه) is attached to (منيبا). (ثُمَّ إِذا خَوَّلَهُ نِعْمَةً مِنْهُ نَسِيَ ما كانَ يَدْعُوا إِلَيْهِ مِنْ قَبْلُ) (ثم) is a conjunction of delay; (إذا) is an adverb of future time containing the meaning of a condition; the clause (خوله) is in the position of the genitive by the adverb's being annexed to it; (خوله) is a past verb, its agent a latent pronoun referring to Allah the Exalted, the (هاء) its first object and (نعمة) its second object; (منه) is an adjective of (نعمة), and you may attach it to (خوّله). The clause (نسي) has no grammatical position, and its agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "he", referring to the human being; (ما) is a direct object; the clause (كان) is the ṣila of (ما); the subject of (كان) is a latent pronoun referring to the human being; the clause (يدعو) is the khabar of (كان); (إليه) is attached to (يدعو); and (من قبل) is attached to an omitted ḥāl. It is permissible for (ما) to be a maṣdar particle, that is, "he forgot his having been a supplicant".
(وَجَعَلَ لِلَّهِ أَنْداداً لِيُضِلَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِهِ) (وجعل) is conjoined to (نسي), and its agent is a latent pronoun referring to the human being; (لله) is attached to an omitted word which is the second object of (جعل); (أندادا) is the first object of (جعل); the (لام) of (ليضل) is of reason, and (يضل) is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied (أن) after the lām. It was also said that the lām is of consequence, which fits with the reading (يَضِلَّ) with fatḥa on the first letter; both are among the seven canonical readings. (عن سبيله) is attached to (يضل). (قُلْ تَمَتَّعْ بِكُفْرِكَ قَلِيلًا إِنَّكَ مِنْ أَصْحابِ النَّارِ) (قل) is an imperative verb with a latent agent, its implied form being "you"; (تمتع) is also an imperative verb with a latent agent, and the clause is the content of the saying. The command is intended as a threat. (بكفرك) is attached to (تمتع); (قليلا) is an adverb of time or a mafʿūl muṭlaq, an adjective of an omitted maṣdar. The clause (إنك من أصحاب النار) gives the reason for the command to enjoy; (إن) and its subject, and (من أصحاب النار) is its khabar.

dervis-irab:9-10.t:
* Vocabulary:
(قانِتٌ): one who performs the duties of obedience and its obligations. From it is the saying of the Prophet ﷺ: «The best prayer is the long qunūt», which means standing in it; and from it is the qunūt in the witr prayer, because it is the supplication of the one praying while standing. In al-Qāmūs: «Al-qunūt: obedience, silence, supplication, standing in prayer, and refraining from speech. Aqnata: he supplicated against his enemy, prolonged his standing in prayer, persisted in pilgrimage, prolonged the campaign, and humbled himself to Allah the Exalted. A woman qanīt is clearly of qanāt, eating little; and a waterskin qanīt is musayyak (holds water well).» Al-Qāmūs's word musayyak is with kasra on the mīm and sukūn on the sīn, meaning it holds water. [Translator's note: the closing quotation mark is placed here, as the source does not mark it.]
(آناءَ): the plural of ini (with kasra on the hamza and a short vowel), like miʿan (with kasra on the mīm and a short vowel), whose plural is amʿāʾ. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «Al-ānāʾ, on the pattern of afʿāl, are the times, and for its singular there are two forms: ini with kasra on the hamza and a short vowel, and ini on the pattern of ḥaml.» In al-Mukhtār: «Ānāʾ al-layl are its hours. Al-Akhfash said that the singular is ini, like miʿan; it was also said that the singular is ini and inw. One says: two or two "anyān" and "anwān" of the night have passed.» [Translator's note: the closing quotation mark is missing in the source; and the vowelling of the singular forms is rendered only approximately here since the source gives it in words.]

* I'rab:
(أَمَّنْ هُوَ قانِتٌ آناءَ اللَّيْلِ ساجِداً وَقائِماً يَحْذَرُ الْآخِرَةَ وَيَرْجُوا رَحْمَةَ رَبِّهِ) (أم) may be a connected conjunction whose counterpart is omitted, its implied form being "the disbeliever is better, or the one who is devout?", and it has entered upon the relative (من), so the mīm was assimilated into the mīm. Or it is a disconnected one, and is then rendered as "rather" plus the hamza, that is, "rather, is the one who is devout like others?". It was also read with the lightened form, in which the hamza is for rebuking interrogation. In every case, (من) is a relative noun, a mubtadaʾ whose khabar is omitted as above; (هو) is mubtadaʾ and (قانت) its khabar, and the clause is the ṣila of (من); (آناء الليل) is an adverb attached to (قانت); (ساجدا) is a ḥāl and (قائما) is conjoined to it; the clause (يحذر الآخرة) is a third ḥāl; and the clause (يرجو رحمة ربه) is conjoined to the clause (يحذر الآخرة).
(قُلْ هَلْ يَسْتَوِي الَّذِينَ يَعْلَمُونَ وَالَّذِينَ لا يَعْلَمُونَ) (هل) is an interrogative particle whose meaning is denial; (يستوي) is an imperfect verb and (الذين) its agent; the clause (يعلمون) is the ṣila; and (والذين لا يعلمون) is conjoined to (الذين يعلمون). In this verse a transitive verb is treated as an intransitive, and the object of (يعلمون) is not supplied, because the implied is like the present, that is, "are those for whom the reality of knowledge has been established and those for whom it has not been established equal?" The question is one of denial, that is, the two are not equal, because the aim is to state the verb's being established for its agent, not its falling upon an object. The point that distinguishes the treated-as-intransitive from other usage is that your saying "so-and-so gives" is to state that he is a giver, which is speech with one who is ignorant of the very fact of giving, whereas your saying "so-and-so gives dinars" is to state the kind of thing that the giving takes, not to state that he is a giver, and is speech with one for whom the fact of giving is established, not with one ignorant of giving. (إِنَّما يَتَذَكَّرُ أُولُوا الْأَلْبابِ) (إنما) is a restricting particle with what it restricts; (يتذكر) is an imperfect nominative verb; (أولو الألباب) is the agent; and the sentence is resumptive, to show that the preceding blows and warnings had no effect on their hearts, owing to the impairment of their minds.
(قُلْ يا عِبادِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمْ) (يا) is a vocative particle; (عبادي) is a vocative muḍāf; (الذين) is an adjective of (عبادي); the clause (آمنوا) is the ṣila of (الذين); and the sentence is the content of the saying. (اتقوا ربكم) is an imperative verb, an agent and a direct object. (لِلَّذِينَ أَحْسَنُوا فِي هذِهِ الدُّنْيا حَسَنَةٌ وَأَرْضُ اللَّهِ واسِعَةٌ) (للذين) is a fronted khabar; the clause (أحسنوا) is the ṣila; (في هذه) is attached to (أحسنوا); (الدنيا) is a badal of the demonstrative noun; (حسنة) is the deferred mubtadaʾ; (أرض الله) is a mubtadaʾ; and (واسعة) the khabar. (إِنَّما يُوَفَّى الصَّابِرُونَ أَجْرَهُمْ بِغَيْرِ حِسابٍ) The sentence gives the reason for what precedes, to encourage patience. (إنما) is a restricting particle with what it restricts; (الصابرون) is the deputy agent; (أجرهم) is a second direct object; and (بغير حساب) is a ḥāl from (الأجر).
Even if there were nothing in patience but what came in this verse, it would suffice. In the ḥadīth: «Waiting for relief with patience is worship.» It was said to ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib: what is nearest to disbelief? He said: one in need who has no patience. Among their sayings: «Patience is bitter, only a free man swallows it.» ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Muqaffaʿ used to say: «When a grave matter befalls you, look: if you have a device for it, do not be helpless, and if it is of what there is no device for, do not be anxious.» How fine is his saying "be helpless" and "be anxious" (تعجز وتجزع): this is what is called qalb al-baʿḍ (partial inversion), and it is counted by the masters of badīʿ among the forms of jinās (paronomasia).

dervis-irab:11-18.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ إِنِّي أُمِرْتُ أَنْ أَعْبُدَ اللَّهَ مُخْلِصاً لَهُ الدِّينَ) (إن) and its subject; the clause (أمرت) is its khabar, and the sentence is the content of the saying. (أمرت) is a past passive verb and the (تاء) is the deputy agent. (أن) and what is within its scope is accusative by removal of the preposition, attached to (أمرت). (مخلصا) is a ḥāl; (له) is attached to (مخلصا); and (الدين) is a direct object.
(وَأُمِرْتُ لِأَنْ أَكُونَ أَوَّلَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ) (وأمرت) is conjoined to the first (أمرت). (لأن أكون) is attached to (أمرت), that is, "to be", so the (لام) has the meaning of the (باء); the subject of (أكون) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "I". It was also said that the lām is of reason, that is, "in order that I be". Al-Zamakhsharī has a lengthy exposition on this point, which we quote in the section on benefits because of its importance. (أول) is the khabar of (أكون), and (المسلمين) is a muḍāf ilayhi. (قُلْ إِنِّي أَخافُ إِنْ عَصَيْتُ رَبِّي عَذابَ يَوْمٍ عَظِيمٍ) (إن) and its subject; the clause (أخاف) is the khabar, and the agent of (أخاف) is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "I". (إن) is conditional; (عصيت) is a verb and agent, and it is in the position of the jussive as the protasis; the apodosis is omitted, indicated by what precedes, that is, "then I fear". (عذاب يوم) is the object of (أخاف), and (عظيم) is an adjective of (يوم).
(قُلِ اللَّهَ أَعْبُدُ مُخْلِصاً لَهُ دِينِي) The sacred name is a fronted object of (أعبد); (أعبد) is an imperfect verb with a latent agent, its implied form being "I"; (مخلصا) is a ḥāl; (له) is attached to (مخلصا); and (ديني) is the object of (مخلصا), that is, that it may be free from association, ostentation, and everything that mixes with deeds and spoils them. (فَاعْبُدُوا ما شِئْتُمْ مِنْ دُونِهِ) The (فاء) is the eloquent (fāʾ al-faṣīḥa); (اعبدوا) is an imperative verb whose purpose is threat and menace, and the (واو) is the agent; (ما) is a direct object; the clause (شئتم) is the ṣila; and (من دونه) is a ḥāl.
