(قُلْ إِنَّ الْخاسِرِينَ الَّذِينَ خَسِرُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ وَأَهْلِيهِمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ) (إن) and its subject; (الذين) is its khabar; the clause (خسروا) is the ṣila of (الذين); (أنفسهم) is a direct object; (أهليهم) is conjoined to (أنفسهم); and (يوم القيامة) is an adverb of (خسروا) or a ḥāl from (أهليهم), meaning their wives and servants. (أَلا ذلِكَ هُوَ الْخُسْرانُ الْمُبِينُ) (ألا) is a particle of alerting; (ذلك) is mubtadaʾ; (هو) is a second mubtadaʾ; (الخسران) is the khabar of (هو); the sentence is the khabar of (ذلك); and (المبين) is an adjective of (الخسران). You may make (هو) a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) with no grammatical position. More will be said about this verse in the section on rhetoric.
(لَهُمْ مِنْ فَوْقِهِمْ ظُلَلٌ مِنَ النَّارِ وَمِنْ تَحْتِهِمْ ظُلَلٌ) (لهم) is a fronted khabar; (من فوقهم) is a ḥāl; (ظلل) is a deferred mubtadaʾ. There is a vagueness in the speech, the explanation of which will come in the section on rhetoric. (من النار) is an adjective of (ظلل); and (من تحتهم ظلل) is conjoined to (من فوقهم ظلل). (ذلِكَ يُخَوِّفُ اللَّهُ بِهِ عِبادَهُ يا عِبادِ فَاتَّقُونِ) (ذلك) is a mubtadaʾ, that is, that punishment; the clause (يخوف الله به) is the khabar; (عباده) is the object of (يخوف). (يا) is a vocative particle; (عباد) is a vocative muḍāf to the first-person yāʾ which has been omitted in conformity with the written form of the Qur'anic text. The (فاء) is the eloquent (fāʾ al-faṣīḥa); (اتقون) is an imperative verb; the (واو) is the agent; the nūn is the protective nūn; and the first-person yāʾ, omitted for the reason given, is the direct object. (وَالَّذِينَ اجْتَنَبُوا الطَّاغُوتَ أَنْ يَعْبُدُوها وَأَنابُوا إِلَى اللَّهِ لَهُمُ الْبُشْرى) (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (اجتنبوا) is the ṣila; (الطاغوت) is a direct object. This has been discussed already, namely that it is used for the singular and the plural and for the masculine and the feminine. (أن يعبدوها) is an interpreted maṣdar in the position of the accusative as a badal of inclusion (badal ishtimāl) from (الطاغوت), that is, "worship of it". More about (الطاغوت) will come in the section on rhetoric. (لهم) is a fronted khabar; (البشرى) is a deferred mubtadaʾ; and the nominal sentence is the khabar of (الذين).
(فَبَشِّرْ عِبادِ) The (فاء) is the eloquent (fāʾ al-faṣīḥa); (بشر) is an imperative verb with a latent agent, its implied form being "you"; (عباد) is a direct object, with the sign of the accusative being a fatḥa implied on the letter before the first-person yāʾ, which is omitted in conformity with the written form of the text. In it the pronoun is made explicit, that is, "so give them good tidings", out of concern for them. (الَّذِينَ يَسْتَمِعُونَ الْقَوْلَ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ أَحْسَنَهُ) (الذين) is an adjective of (عباد); the clause (يستمعون) is the ṣila; (القول) is a direct object; the (فاء) is a conjunction; (يتبعون) is conjoined to (يستمعون); and (أحسنه) is a direct object. (أُولئِكَ الَّذِينَ هَداهُمُ اللَّهُ وَأُولئِكَ هُمْ أُولُوا الْأَلْبابِ) (أولئك) is a mubtadaʾ and (الدين) [Translator's note: the source reads «الدين», evidently for «الذين»] is the khabar; the reference is to those described by what was mentioned; the clause (هداهم الله) is the ṣila. (وأولئك) is a mubtadaʾ; (هم) is a second mubtadaʾ or a separating pronoun; (أولو الألباب) is the khabar of (هم), and the sentence is the khabar of (أولئك), or it is the khabar of (أولئك).

* Rhetoric:
1- Intimidation (tahwīl):
In His words «ألا ذلك هو الخسران المبين» there is an excellent intimidation. He made the sentence resumptive and headed it with the particle of alerting; He placed the separating pronoun between the mubtadaʾ and the khabar; and He made "loss" definite, as though it were something whose matter is familiar and whose terror is well known; and He described it as "manifest", thereby making their loss the extreme of horror and the utmost of ugliness.
2- Hyperbole:
In likening the Devil to (الطاغوت) there are three aspects of hyperbole:
1- Naming him by the maṣdar, as though he were tyranny itself.
2- Building it on the pattern faʿlūt, which is a pattern of hyperbole, like raḥmūt, which is wide mercy, and malakūt, which is wide dominion.
3- The third likeness is the fronting of its lām before its ʿayn, to convey its being specific to this naming.

* Benefits:
We promised you to quote the delightful passage that al-Zamakhsharī wrote on the i'rab of His words «إني أمرت أن أعبد الله مخلصا له الدين، وأمرت لأن أكون من المسلمين». He said: «If you ask: how is "I was commanded" joined to "I was commanded" when they are one? I say: they are not one, because of the difference of their two aspects. The command to be sincere, and the obligation of it, is one thing; and the command to it so that the one who stands by it may take the lead in the race in religion is another thing. When two aspects of a thing differ and are separate, it takes the place of two different things. You may also make the lām an addition, like it is in "I wanted to do" (أردت لأن أفعل), and it is not added except with (أن) specifically, not with a plain noun, as though it were added as a compensation for leaving the original for what takes its place, as the sīn was made a compensation in (اسطاع) for leaving the original, which is (أطوع). The evidence for this aspect is its coming without a lām in His words "and I was commanded to be of the Muslims" and "I was commanded to be of the believers". "That I be the first to submit" has several aspects in its meaning: that I be the first to submit in my time and of my people, because he was the first to oppose the religion of his forefathers and cast off the idols and smash them; that I be the first of those whom I have called to Islam in my own submission; and that I be the first to call himself to what he calls others to, so that I may be followed in my word and deed together, and my description may not be that of kings, who command what they do not do; and that I do what makes me deserve priority from the deeds of the foremost, as an indication of the cause by the effect.» Ponder it, for it is among the choicest of sayings. [Translator's note: the source places the closing quotation mark before «فتأمله»; the translation follows it.]

dervis-irab:53-59.t:
* I'rab:
(قُلْ يا عِبادِيَ الَّذِينَ أَسْرَفُوا عَلى أَنْفُسِهِمْ لا تَقْنَطُوا مِنْ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ) A resumptive statement, brought to show that turning back [to Allah] is required, since the latitude for the transgressor is great. يا عبادي is an annexed vocative, annexed to the first-person yāʾ which carries a fatḥa; it was also read «يا عباد» with the yāʾ dropped, after a kasra; the rule of a vocative annexed to the first-person yāʾ has preceded. الذين is an adjective (naʿt) of عبادي; the clause أسرفوا is the ṣila; على أنفسهم is attached to أسرفوا; لا is prohibitive; تقنطوا is an imperfect verb jussive by لا, and the wāw is the agent; من رحمة الله is attached to تقنطوا. The verb قنط belongs to the pattern تعب and the pattern سلم, so a kasra or a fatḥa is permissible on its nūn in the imperfect, and both have been read. In al-Mukhtār: «القنوط is despair; its verb pattern is جلس, دخل, طرب and سلم; so he is قنط, قنوط and قانط.» It has also been read with a ḍamma, irregularly.
(إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ جَمِيعاً إِنَّهُ هُوَ الْغَفُورُ الرَّحِيمُ) inna with its noun, and the clause يغفر is its khabar (predicate); the clause is the reason for the prohibition of despair, and therefore it has been said: this is the most hope-giving verse in the Qur'an; the rhetorical artistry it contains will come. الذنوب is a mafʿūl bihi (direct object); جميعا is a ḥāl (circumstantial); and that is after repentance from polytheism. inna with its noun; هو is a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) or a mubtadaʾ; الغفور الرحيم are two khabars of inna or of هو, and the clause is the khabar of inna. (وَأَنِيبُوا إِلى رَبِّكُمْ وَأَسْلِمُوا لَهُ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَكُمُ الْعَذابُ ثُمَّ لا تُنْصَرُونَ) The wāw is a conjunction; أنيبوا is an imperative verb with its agent; إلى ربكم is attached to أنيبوا; وأسلموا is also conjoined; له is attached to أسلموا; من قبل is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl; أن with what is in its scope is an interpreted maṣdar, annexed to the adverb; يأتيكم is an imperfect verb made accusative by أن, the kāf being a fronted direct object and العذاب a postponed agent; ثم is a conjunction of sequence with delay; and «تؤمرون» «[Translator's note: the source prints «تؤمرون», but the verse reads «لا تنصرون»; the explanation that follows concerns «تنصرون»]» is an imperfect verb in the nominative because it is not conjoined to يأتيكم, and the secret of that will come in the section on Rhetoric.
(وَاتَّبِعُوا أَحْسَنَ ما أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْكُمْ مِنْ رَبِّكُمْ) واتبعوا is conjoined to وأنيبوا; أحسن is the direct object of اتبعوا; ما is a relative noun annexed to أحسن; the clause أنزل إليكم is the ṣila; من ربكم is also attached to أنزل. (مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ يَأْتِيَكُمُ الْعَذابُ بَغْتَةً وَأَنْتُمْ لا تَشْعُرُونَ) من قبل is attached to an omitted element as a ḥāl; أن with what is in its scope is in the position of the genitive by annexation; بغتة is a ḥāl; the wāw is circumstantial; أنتم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause لا تشعرون its khabar, and the clause is accusative as a ḥāl.
(أَنْ تَقُولَ نَفْسٌ يا حَسْرَتى عَلى ما فَرَّطْتُ فِي جَنْبِ اللَّهِ) أن with what is in its scope is in the position of the accusative as a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose); al-Zamakhsharī assumed it as "for fear that it says", and Abū l-Baqāʾ assumed «we have warned you for fear that it says» «[Translator's note: the source prints «أنذر ناكم», with a space]»; نفس is the agent of تقول (the secret of its indefiniteness will come in the section on Rhetoric); يا is a vocative particle; حسرتا is an annexed vocative, annexed to the first-person yāʾ which has turned into an alif, its origin being «يا حسرتي», i.e. my regret; على ما فرطت means "for my neglect", so ما is a maṣdar particle and the interpreted maṣdar is genitive by على, the preposition and its genitive noun being attached to حسرتا; في جنب الله is attached to فرطت. The discussion of this kināya will come in the section on Rhetoric.
(وَإِنْ كُنْتُ لَمِنَ السَّاخِرِينَ) The wāw is circumstantial; إن is the light form of the heavy inna, i.e. "while I was"; kāna with its noun; the distinguishing lām (al-lām al-fāriqa); من الساخرين is the khabar of كنت; the clause is accusative in position as a ḥāl. (أَوْ تَقُولَ لَوْ أَنَّ اللَّهَ هَدانِي لَكُنْتُ مِنَ الْمُتَّقِينَ) أو is a conjunction; تقول is conjoined to أن تقول; لو is conditional; أنّ with what is in its scope is the agent of an omitted verb, its implied form being ثبت; inna with its noun, and the clause هداني is its khabar; the lām falls in the answer to لو; kāna with its noun, and من المتقين is its khabar; the clause has no grammatical position because it is the answer to a non-jussive condition «[Translator's note: the source says «جواب شرط جازم», "the answer of a jussive condition", although لو is not a jussive conditional particle]».
(أَوْ تَقُولَ حِينَ تَرَى الْعَذابَ لَوْ أَنَّ لِي كَرَّةً فَأَكُونَ مِنَ الْمُحْسِنِينَ) أو تقول is conjoined to what precedes; the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "she", referring to نفس; أو is for classification of what the soul says on that hard day, making excuses with what is of no use and yields no benefit; لو is conditional; أنّ with what is in its scope is the agent of an omitted verb; أنّ with its fronted khabar and كرة its postponed noun. فأكون: the fāʾ is a conjunction and أكون is conjoined to كرة, so it is a conjunction onto a pure noun, to be interpreted by a verb, and reference to this has preceded; or the fāʾ is of causation, and أكون is an imperfect verb made accusative by an implied أن after the fāʾ of causation that falls as the answer to wishing, understood from His saying «لو أن لي كرة». The difference between the two aspects is that on the first, "being" is part of what is wished for, while on the second, "being" is consequent upon the attainment of what is wished for, and is not itself wished for.
(بَلى قَدْ جاءَتْكَ آياتِي فَكَذَّبْتَ بِها وَاسْتَكْبَرْتَ وَكُنْتَ مِنَ الْكافِرِينَ) بلى is a particle of reply, coming to refute the negation contained in the speaker's saying «لو أن الله هداني»; قد is a particle of affirmation; جاءتك آياتي is a verb, direct object and agent; فكذبت بها is conjoined to جاءتك; كنت is kāna with its noun, and من الكافرين is its khabar.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His saying: «قل يا عبادي الذين أسرفوا على أنفسهم لا تقنطوا من رحمة الله إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعا إنه هو الغفور الرحيم» are various arts of the sciences of badīʿ and bayān, which we summarize as follows: 1- His turning towards them, Glorified is He, in which is the utmost reassurance for them, to wipe out their past sins and stains, and the signal that they have ample time ahead to make up for what they neglected and mend what was broken.
2- Calling them, in which is such affection and gentleness toward them as urges those of them with sound reason to hasten to turn back and return in repentance.
3- Annexing them to Himself with an annexation of honor, and that they are fit, through the bond of servanthood by which they are related to Him, Glorified is He; and that suffices for them to respond in kind and to announce repentance in order to draw near to Him through it.
4- Annexing mercy to His most particular and most majestic name, and [showing] that it is the basis of His dealing with His servants.
5- Repeating the overt noun in its own wording in His saying «إن الله يغفر الذنوب جميعا».
6- The iltifāt (shift) from the first person to the third in His saying «من رحمة الله», to specify mercy with the noble Name, as was said above.
7- Presenting the clause «إنه هو الغفور الرحيم» reinforced with inna, with the separating pronoun and with the two attributes that hold intensity. These are seven complete arts in a single verse.
2- Al-Īḍāḥ (clarification):
That is in His saying «ثم لا تنصرون». Someone may ask: why was تنصرون not conjoined to «أن يأتيكم», which is accusative? The answer to this difficulty is that He intended, and He knows best, a promise by informing them that He will never help them in the future so long as they persist in not turning back and hold back from submission. A similar verse has preceded in this art, in Sūrat Āl ʿImrān.
3- Indefiniteness (tankīr):
The secret of the indefiniteness of نفس in His saying «أن تقول نفس» is smallness in number, because what is meant by it is some souls, namely the soul of the disbeliever, which is distinguished from other souls by this trait of obstinacy in disbelief. It may be that abundance was intended by it, as in the saying of al-Aʿshā:
ورب بقيع لو هتفت بجوه ... أتاني كريم ينفض الرأس مغضبا (How many a spacious valley, had I called out in its midst, a noble man would have come to me, shaking his head in anger.)
He means many noble men, not one noble man. Similar is: رب بلد قطعت (many a land have I crossed), ورب بطل قارعت (many a hero have I fought), where he means many lands and many heroes.
4- Kināya (metonymy):
In His saying «على ما فرطت في جنب الله»; الجنب means "side". One says: "I am in the side of so-and-so", his side and his region; and "so-and-so is soft of side and flank"; then they said "he was neglectful in his side" and "in his flank", meaning in his right. Jamīl ibn Maʿmar said:
أما تتقين الله في جنب وامق ... له كبد حرى عليك تقطع (Do you not fear Allah regarding a lover, whose burning liver is being torn apart for you,)
غريب مشوق مولع بادكاركم ... وكل غريب الدار بالشوق مولع (a stranger, yearning, devoted to remembering you; and every stranger far from home is devoted to yearning?)
Jamīl is appealing to his beloved Buthayna and lamenting to her what has befallen him because of her, that is: "Do you not fear Allah regarding a lover" meaning in his due right which is incumbent upon you; so الجنب is a kināya for that. الوامق is the one of intense love, meaning himself; حرى means having heat and burning; تقطع: its origin is تتقطع; الادكار: its origin is الاذتكار, the tāʾ of iftiʿāl having been turned into an unpointed dāl and the pointed dhāl assimilated into it. He addressed her with the masculine plural address as a sign of respect for her; and in the second verse there is radd al-ʿajuz ʿalā l-ṣadr (the return of the end to the beginning), which is among fine speech. This kināya is called kināyat nisba (kināya of attribution), and the divisions of kināya have preceded, because if you establish a matter in the place of a man and his space, you have established it in him. Ziyād al-Aʿjam said:
إن السماحة والمروءة والندى ... في قبة ضربت على ابن الحشرج (Generosity, manliness and bounty are in a tent pitched over Ibn al-Ḥashraj.)
He means that he is singled out with these traits, which are not found in anyone else; there is no tent there and none was pitched at all.

* Benefits:
The alif of separation (alif al-faṣl):
The alif of separation is added after the wāw of the plural, for fear of its being confused with the wāw of conjunction, such as «وأنيبوا إلى ربكم وأسلموا له» and such as كفروا and وردوا. Do you not see that had they not inserted the alif after the wāw, and then it were joined to speech after it, the reader would think it was كفر and ورد, so the wāw was set apart from what follows by the alif of separation. And since they did this in verbs whose wāw is detached from the letters before it, such as ساروا and جاءوا, they did it in verbs whose wāw is joined to the letters before it, such as كانوا and بانوا, so that the rule of this wāw would be one rule in every place. «[Translator's note: the source prints «فغلوا» in "ولما فغلوا ذلك", a typographical slip for «فعلوا»]»

dervis-irab:19-21.t:
* Vocabulary:
(يَنابِيعَ): In al-Mukhtār: «Nabaʿa al-māʾ: the water came out; its pattern is qaṭaʿa and dakhala. Nabaʿa yanbiʿu with kasra, nabaʿānan with fatḥa on the bāʾ, is also a dialect. Al-yanbūʿ is the spring of water, and from it is His saying the Exalted "until you cause to gush forth for us from the earth a spring" (حتى تفجر لنا من الأرض ينبوعا), and the plural is al-yanābīʿ.» What the common people say, "nabʿ" [Translator's note: for the spring], is a later coinage and not known; rather al-nabʿ is a maṣdar, and a tree from which arrows and bows are made. It is said: "they struck nabʿ with nabʿ", that is, they met and thrust at one another; and "I have not seen anything harder than it as nabʿ", that is, more severe.
(يَهِيجُ): it dries and its dryness is complete, because when its dryness is complete it is time for it to rise up from where it grew and go away. In al-Mukhtār: «Hāja al-nabt yahīju hiyājan with kasra: it dried up.» In al-Miṣbāḥ: «Hāja al-baql yahīju: it turned yellow.»
(حُطاماً): crumbled pieces. In al-Miṣbāḥ: «Ḥaṭama al-shayʾ ḥaṭman, on the pattern of taʿiba, so it is ḥaṭim when it is broken to pieces. A beast is called ḥaṭima when it grows old. It is transitive with the movement: one says ḥaṭamtuhu ḥaṭman, on the pattern of ḍaraba, so it was broken (inḥaṭama); and ḥaṭṭamtuhu, with shadda, is intensive.»

* I'rab:
(أَفَمَنْ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ كَلِمَةُ الْعَذابِ أَفَأَنْتَ تُنْقِذُ مَنْ فِي النَّارِ) The hamza is for rebuking interrogation, and the (فاء) is a conjunction upon an omitted element indicated by the context, the implied form being "Are you the master of their affair, so that the one upon whom the punishment has become due, you rescue him?" (من) is conditional or relative, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is omitted. Abū al-Baqāʾ implied it as "like the one who was saved"; al-Zamakhsharī implied it as "then you are his deliverer", omitted because of what indicates it, "Will you rescue him?"; and another implied "you grieve over him". The second hamza is for interrogation and was repeated to confirm the denial; the (فاء) is a linking particle; (أنت) is mubtadaʾ; the clause (تنقذ) is the khabar; and (من في النار) is the direct object. The overt noun, "the one who is in the Fire", has been put in the place of the pronoun, as if the original were "Will you rescue him?"; (أنت) is mubtadaʾ, the clause (تنقذ) is the khabar, and (من في النار) is its object, so that on this the verse is one sentence. An objection was raised that it combines interrogation and condition, but there is no ground for this objection, because the interrogative particle enters upon an omitted sentence to which the conditional sentence is joined, and it did not enter upon the conditional sentence. More will be said about this verse in the section on rhetoric. (لكِنِ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا رَبَّهُمْ لَهُمْ غُرَفٌ مِنْ فَوْقِها غُرَفٌ مَبْنِيَّةٌ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهارُ) (لكن) is a conjunction and a particle of turning away (iḍrāb), with the meaning of "rather" (بل), and it is not for rectification (istidrāk), because no negation precedes it; the speech is a turning away from one topic to another, different from the first. (الذين) is a mubtadaʾ; the clause (اتقوا) is the ṣila; (ربهم) is a direct object; (لهم) is a fronted khabar; (غرف) is a deferred mubtadaʾ; and the nominal sentence is the khabar of (الذين). (مبنية) is an adjective of (غرف), that is, built in the manner of dwellings; and the clause (تجري من تحتها الأنهار) is a second adjective or a ḥāl from (غرف).
(وَعْدَ اللَّهِ لا يُخْلِفُ اللَّهُ الْمِيعادَ) (وعد الله) is a confirming maṣdar of an omitted verb indicated by His words (لهم غرف), because it is in the sense of "Allah promised them that"; (لا) is negative; (يخلف الله الميعاد) is an imperfect verb, an agent and a direct object. (أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ أَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّماءِ ماءً فَسَلَكَهُ يَنابِيعَ فِي الْأَرْضِ) A resumptive statement, intended as a parable for the life of this world and the swiftness of its passing. The hamza is for affirmative interrogation; (لم) is a particle of negation, inversion and jussive; (تر) is an imperfect verb made jussive by (لم), the sign of its jussive being the omission of the weak letter, and the agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you". (أن) and what is within its scope stands in the place of the two objects of (تر), or its single object, because it is a verb of the heart or of sight. (أن) and its subject; the clause (أنزل) is its khabar; (من السماء) is attached to (أنزل); and (ماء) is a direct object. (فسلكه): the (فاء) is a conjunction; (سلك) is a past verb indeclinable on the fatḥa, its agent a latent pronoun, its implied form being "He", referring to Allah the Exalted. (ينابيع), if it is in the sense of "the place of springing", is an adverb of the omitted maṣdar, that is, "He made it pass in springs"; then, when it was put in the place of the maṣdar, its accusative was made as a maṣdar. If it is in the sense of "the one that gushes", its accusative is as a ḥāl, that is, "gushing". Al-Shihāb al-Khafājī objected to the ḥāl reading and said: «The ḥāl reading is not free of murkiness, because then it ought to be said "from the earth" rather than "in the earth"; and on both aspects "in the earth" is an adjective of (ينابيع).» I say: I see no objection to making (ينابيع) accusative as a tamyīz (specification), on the pattern of His words «وفجرنا الأرض عيونا» ("and We caused the earth to burst forth in springs"); none of those who took up the i'rab of the Qur'an mentioned it, and the explicit sense of al-Zamakhsharī's words supports this i'rab. He said: «springs, channels and courses like veins in bodies.» Many held back from parsing (ينابيع) because of its subtlety. In al-Shawkānī: «"Fa-salakahu yanābīʿa fī al-arḍ": that is, He made it enter and dwell in it. Al-yanābīʿ is the plural of yanbūʿ, from nabaʿa al-māʾ yanbuʿu. Al-yanbūʿ is the spring of water, and the places in which water springs. On the second aspect it is accusative by removal of the preposition. Muqātil said: He made it springs and wells in the earth.» (ثُمَّ يُخْرِجُ بِهِ زَرْعاً مُخْتَلِفاً أَلْوانُهُ) (ثم) is a conjunction of order with delay; (يخرج) is an imperfect verb, and the departure to it from the past, as the style of conjunction requires, is to make the scene present. (به) is attached to (يخرج); (زرعا) is a direct object; (مختلفا) is an adjective of (زرعا); and (ألوانه) is the agent of (مختلف). (ثُمَّ يَهِيجُ فَتَراهُ مُصْفَرًّا) (ثم يهيج) is conjoined to (ثم يخرج); (فتراه): the (فاء) is a conjunction, the (هاء) a direct object, and (مصفرا) a ḥāl, because the seeing is by sight. (ثُمَّ يَجْعَلُهُ حُطاماً إِنَّ فِي ذلِكَ لَذِكْرى لِأُولِي الْأَلْبابِ) Conjoined to what precedes. (يجعله حطاما) is an imperfect verb with a latent agent; the (هاء) is the first direct object and (حطاما) the second; (إن) is a particle resembling the verb; (في ذلك) is its fronted khabar; the (لام) is the shifted lām; (ذكرى) is its deferred subject; and (لأولي الألباب) is an adjective of (ذكرى) or is attached to the very reminder, because it means "admonition".

* Rhetoric:
In His words «أفأنت تنقذ من في النار» there is a mursal majāz (unrestricted metaphor) whose relation is causality: the cause is mentioned and the effect is meant. The meaning is: will you guide him by your calling him to faith, and so rescue him from the Fire?

dervis-irab:60-66.t:
* Vocabulary:
(بمفازة): المفازة is the deadly desert, named by the name of "deliverance" as a good omen. فوّز المسافر means the traveller rode into the mafāza and went on in it. Ḥassān said:
لله درّ رافع أنّى اهتدى ... فوّز من قراقر إلى سوى (To Allah belongs the merit of Rāfiʿ, how was he guided? He crossed the desert from Qarāqir to Suwā.)
فوّز بإبله means he crossed with his camels; فوّز الرجل means the man died, and so found himself in a mafāza, the stretch between this world and the other, the extended barzakh; or because المفازة became a name for the place of destruction, from it فوّز was taken in the sense of "perished". فاز سهمه and خرج له سهم فائز mean the arrow won; فاز بفائزة هنيّة وأجيز بجائزة سنية means he gained a pleasant gain and was given a lofty prize. They also called the snake-bitten man سليم ("sound") as a good omen of his recovery, as they called the caravan of travellers قافلة ("returning") as a good omen of their return.
(مَقالِيدُ): المقاليد is the plural of مقلاد like مفتاح (pl. مفاتيح), or of مقليد like منديل (pl. مناديل), and the speech is of the kināya type. The wording of al-Qāmūs is:
«الإقليد is the ring in the camel's nostril, and the key, like المقلاد and المقلد; and a strip with which the head of the basket is bound; and something made long, such as a thread of brass, hung on the nose-ring and on the ring of the earring, like القلاد and the neck; its plural is أقلاد. ناقة قلداء means a long-necked she-camel. And like سكيت and مصباح: the treasury. ضاقت مقالده ومقاليده means his affairs became constricted for him. And like منبر: the container, the feed-bag, the measure, and a staff with a curve at its head» up to where he says: «والقلادة is what is placed on the neck, and تقلد means he put it on.» Yet al-Zamakhsharī and other scholars of language say that the origin of the word is Persian. He says in al-Kashshāf: «"له مقاليد السموات والأرض" means He is the owner of their affair and their keeper, and this is of the kināya type, because the keeper of treasuries and manager of their affair is the one who holds their keys; of this is their saying "I cast to him the keys (مقاليد) of the kingdom", and these are the keys, and they have no singular from their own wording; it is also said مقلد, and one says إقليد and أقاليد. The word is originally Persian. If you ask: what has the clear Arabic Book to do with Persian? I say: Arabization turned it into Arabic, just as use took out the neglected [word] from being neglected.»

* I'rab:
(وَيَوْمَ الْقِيامَةِ تَرَى الَّذِينَ كَذَبُوا عَلَى اللَّهِ وُجُوهُهُمْ مُسْوَدَّةٌ) The wāw is resumptive; the adverb is attached to ترى; ترى is an imperfect nominative verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; الذين is its direct object; the clause كذبوا على الله is the ṣila; وجوههم is a mubtadaʾ (subject) and مسودة its khabar (predicate); the nominal clause is in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the relative noun, because the sight is visual. It is also possible that the sight is of the heart, in which case the clause is in the place of the second object of ترى. "Lying against Allah" means ascribing a partner to Him. (أَلَيْسَ فِي جَهَنَّمَ مَثْوىً لِلْمُتَكَبِّرِينَ) The hamza is for affirmative interrogation (istifhām taqrīrī); ليس and its fronted khabar; مثوى is its postponed noun; للمتكبرين is an adjective (naʿt) of مثوى, and the clause gives the reason for the blackening of their faces. (وَيُنَجِّي اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا بِمَفازَتِهِمْ) The wāw is a conjunction; ينجي الله الذين is an imperfect verb, agent and direct object; the clause اتقوا is the ṣila; بمفازتهم is attached to ينجي because it indicates cause: their winning of success is the cause of deliverance. (لا يَمَسُّهُمُ السُّوءُ وَلا هُمْ يَحْزَنُونَ) لا is negative; يمسهم السوء is an imperfect verb, direct object and agent; the wāw is a conjunction and لا is negative; هم is a mubtadaʾ and the clause يحزنون its khabar. The clause لا يمسهم السوء has no grammatical position because it explains the mafāza, as if it were said: "What is their mafāza?" and it was said "Evil will not touch them". It is not unlikely to be in the position of the accusative as a ḥāl from الذين اتقوا, and al-Zamakhsharī permitted that it be resumptive.
(اللَّهُ خالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَهُوَ عَلى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَكِيلٌ) الله is a mubtadaʾ and خالق كل شيء its khabar; هو is a mubtadaʾ; على كل شيء is attached to وكيل, and وكيل is the khabar of هو, and the clause is resumptive. (لَهُ مَقالِيدُ السَّماواتِ وَالْأَرْضِ) له is a fronted khabar and مقاليد السموات والأرض a postponed mubtadaʾ, and the clause is also resumptive. (وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِآياتِ اللَّهِ أُولئِكَ هُمُ الْخاسِرُونَ) الذين is a mubtadaʾ; the clause كفروا بآيات الله is the ṣila; هم is a mubtadaʾ and الخاسرون its khabar, and the clause is the khabar of الذين; or you may make هم a separating pronoun (ḍamīr faṣl) with no position, as has preceded; the clause is conjoined to «وينجي الله الذين اتقوا», the conjunction of one of two opposites to the other, and the fact that the conjoined clause is nominal and the clause conjoined to is verbal does not prevent this conjunction. (قُلْ: أَفَغَيْرَ اللَّهِ تَأْمُرُونِّي أَعْبُدُ أَيُّهَا الْجاهِلُونَ) The hamza is for rhetorical denial (istifhām inkārī) and the fāʾ is conjoined to an omitted element; غير الله is accusative by أعبد; the clause تأمروني is parenthetical, and the discussion of the omission of the nūn will come; أعبد is an imperfect verb, the original being «تأمرونني أن أعبد», so أن was omitted and أعبد became nominative, as it became nominative in the saying of Ṭarafa:
ألا أيها ذا الزاجري أحضر الوغى ... وأن اشهد اللذات هل أنت مخلدي (O you who rebuke me for attending the battle and for taking part in pleasures, are you going to make me immortal?)
Here is the full text of Abū l-Baqāʾ's i'rab of this verse:
«"أفغير الله": there are several aspects in its i'rab. One: that it is accusative by أعبد, fronted before it. This aspect has been weakened, since the assumed form is «أن أعبد», and that then leads to the fronting of the ṣila before the relative; but this is nothing, because أن is not in the wording, so its operation does not remain; and were we to assume that its rule remains, it would lead to omitting the relative while its ṣila remains, and that is not permitted except in poetic necessity. The second aspect: that it be accusative by تأمروني, with أعبد a substitute for it, the assumption being "Say: do you order me to worship other than Allah, the Mighty and Majestic?"; this is a badal ishtimāl (substitute of inclusion) and of the type «أمرتك الخير». The third: that غير is accusative by an omitted verb, i.e. "Do you impose on me other than Allah?", which the later [verb] explains. It was also said that أعبد has no position in i'rab; and it was said it is a ḥāl. The practice follows the first two aspects. As for the nūn, it is doubled in the original and was lightened by omitting the second; he has mentioned its parallels.» The nūn of تأمروني is the nūn of the nominative, given a kasra for harmony, and the nūn of protection was omitted because of the meeting of two identical letters. It was read with sukūn on the yāʾ and with fatḥa, so the readings are four and all of them are among the seven. أيها is an indefinite specified vocative, indeclinable on the ḍamma, the hāʾ is for alerting, and الجاهلون is a badal of أيها.
(وَلَقَدْ أُوحِيَ إِلَيْكَ وَإِلَى الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِكَ) The lām prepares for an oath (lām muwaṭṭiʾa); قد is a particle of affirmation; أوحي is a passive past verb; إليك takes the place of the deputy agent; it is also said that the deputy agent is omitted, indicated by the course of the speech, i.e. "monotheism was revealed to you"; والى الذين is conjoined to إليك; من قبلك is attached to an omitted element which is the ṣila of the relative. (لَئِنْ أَشْرَكْتَ لَيَحْبَطَنَّ عَمَلُكَ وَلَتَكُونَنَّ مِنَ الْخاسِرِينَ) The lām also prepares for an oath; إن is conditional; أشركت is a past verb in the position of the jussive as the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); the lām falls in the answer to the oath. This oath and its answer are the answer to the first oath, while the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, in line with the saying of Ibn Mālik:
واحذف لدى اجتماع شرط وقسم ... جواب ما أخرت فهو ملتزم (When a condition and an oath meet, omit the answer of the one placed later; that is obligatory.)
ليحبطن is a past verb «[Translator's note: so in the source; the form is actually an imperfect verb]» indeclinable on the fatḥa because of the attachment of the heavy emphatic nūn; عملك is the agent; ولتكونن is conjoined to ليحبطن; the noun of تكونن is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; and من الخاسرين is the khabar. (بَلِ اللَّهَ فَاعْبُدْ وَكُنْ مِنَ الشَّاكِرِينَ) A statement conjoined to an implied element indicated by the context, i.e. "so do not associate partners"; الله is accusative by an omitted verb indicated by فاعبد, i.e. "if you are rational, worship Allah"; the fāʾ is the fāʾ faṣīḥa; اعبد is an imperative verb whose agent is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; وكن is conjoined to اعبد; the noun of كن is a latent pronoun, its implied form being "you"; and من الشاكرين is the khabar of كن.

* Benefits:
Sībawayh devoted a special chapter in his book to this construction, «بل الله فاعبد», and this is its gist: the original is «فاعبد الله»; then they omitted the first verb for brevity. When the fāʾ came first, they disliked beginning with it, since its nature is to stand between the conjoined and that to which it is conjoined; so they fronted the object, and it became medial in wording and indicative that there is an omitted condition which required its presence, so that what follows it be conjoined to it. To this goal in fronting is added the benefit of restriction, as has preceded, from the indication of specification through fronting.

dervis-irab:22-23.t:
* Vocabulary:
(تَقْشَعِرُّ): iqshaʿarra jildahu: he shuddered, contracted, became rough, and his colour changed, so he is muqshaʿirr. Iqshaʿarrat al-sana: the year became barren and dry. Iqshaʿarrat al-arḍ: the earth contracted and drew together when no rain fell upon it. It is said "the hair bristled (iqshaʿarra)", that is, stood upright from fright or cold. The maṣdar is iqshiʿrār. Al-Zamakhsharī said:
«Iqshaʿarra al-jild: when it contracts severely. Its composition is from the letters of al-qashʿ, which is dry hide, with a fourth letter added to them, the rāʾ, so that it is quadriliteral, indicating an additional meaning.» More detail on this root will come in the section on rhetoric. [Translator's note: the closing quotation mark is missing in the source.]

* I'rab:
(أَفَمَنْ شَرَحَ اللَّهُ صَدْرَهُ لِلْإِسْلامِ فَهُوَ عَلى نُورٍ مِنْ رَبِّهِ) A resumptive statement, intended to serve as a reason for what precedes, namely the restriction of the reminder to those of understanding. The hamza is for rebuking interrogation; the (فاء) is a conjunction upon an implied sentence, that is, "are all people equal?" (من) is relative or conditional, in the position of the nominative as mubtadaʾ. On the first view its khabar is omitted, its implied form being "like one whose heart has been sealed"; on the second view its khabar is the protasis and the apodosis together. The (فاء) is a conjunction in either case; (هو) is mubtadaʾ; (على نور) is the khabar; and (من ربه) is an adjective of (نور). (فَوَيْلٌ لِلْقاسِيَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ مِنْ ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ أُولئِكَ فِي ضَلالٍ مُبِينٍ) The (فاء) is a linking particle; (ويل) is a mubtadaʾ, and it is allowed to begin with it because of the sense of invoking punishment and loss in it. (للقاسية) is the khabar; (قلوبهم) is the agent of (للقاسية); and (من ذكر الله) is attached to (القاسية). (من) is either of reason, that is, "on account of the remembrance of Him", or it was said that (من) has the sense of (عن), the meaning being "hardened against accepting the remembrance". (أولئك) is mubtadaʾ and (في ضلال مبين) its khabar. (اللَّهُ نَزَّلَ أَحْسَنَ الْحَدِيثِ كِتاباً مُتَشابِهاً مَثانِيَ) The sacred name is a mubtadaʾ (the secret of the fronting will come in the section on rhetoric), and the clause (نزل أحسن الحديث) is the khabar. (كتابا) is a badal of (أحسن الحديث), and it may be a ḥāl from it, that is, "a Qur'an resembling itself". (متشابها) is a first adjective and (مثاني) a second adjective. The meaning of this word has gone before, and further rhetorical points will come in the section on rhetoric.
(تَقْشَعِرُّ مِنْهُ جُلُودُ الَّذِينَ يَخْشَوْنَ رَبَّهُمْ ثُمَّ تَلِينُ جُلُودُهُمْ وَقُلُوبُهُمْ إِلى ذِكْرِ اللَّهِ) The clause (تقشعر) is a third adjective; (منه) is attached to (تقشعر); (جلود) is the agent; the clause (يخشون ربهم) is the ṣila; (ثم) is a conjunction of delay; (تلين جلودهم) is an imperfect verb and an agent; (قلوبهم) is conjoined to (جلودهم); and (إلى ذكر الله) is attached to (تلين), because it contains the meaning of "become calm and at ease toward the remembrance of Allah".
(ذلِكَ هُدَى اللَّهِ يَهْدِي بِهِ مَنْ يَشاءُ) (ذلك) is a mubtadaʾ and (هدى الله) the khabar, or a badal of the demonstrative noun; the clause (يهدي) is either a ḥāl or a khabar; (به) is attached to (يهدي); (من يشاء) is a direct object; and the clause (يشاء) is the ṣila. The reference is to the Book, so the clause is a ḥāl from it. (وَمَنْ يُضْلِلِ اللَّهُ فَما لَهُ مِنْ هادٍ) The (واو) is resumptive; (من) is a jussive conditional noun in the position of the accusative as a fronted object of (يضلل); (الله) is the agent; the (فاء) is a linking particle; (ما) is negative or a negative of the Ḥijāzī type; (له) is a khabar, or the fronted khabar of (هاد); (من) is a redundant preposition; and (هاد) is a deferred mubtadaʾ, nominative in position, or the subject of (ما), genitive in form, its sign of genitive being an implied kasra on the letter before the yāʾ which is omitted because of the meeting of two quiescent letters.

* Rhetoric:
1- In His words «مثاني»:
The singular is described by the plural because the Book is a whole possessing details. Do you not say: the Qur'an is sevenths and fifths, sūras and verses, stories, rulings and repeated admonitions? Its like is your saying: man is bones, veins and nerves. Al-Zamakhsharī allowed another delicate aspect. He said: «It is possible that (مثاني) is not an adjective but is accusative as a tamyīz of (متشابها), as you say "I saw a man good in his qualities", the meaning being "resembling in its repetitions".»
2- The benefit of repetition:
The benefit of doubling and repetition is to establish the speech in the mind, for souls ordinarily grow weary of admonition and warning and tire of advice at first. So in the repetition of counsel and admonition there is accustoming them to find it agreeable and to act upon it. It is established that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to repeat to them what he preached and advised, three times and sometimes seven, to implant it in their souls; and the sharp teacher does not cease to repeat the lessons he gives his students until they become agreeable to them and tender in their souls, after having been hard and repulsive.
3- Living embodiment:
In His words «تقشعر منه جلود الذين يخشون ربهم ثم تلين جلودهم وقلوبهم إلى ذكر الله» there are wonderful rhetorical points, the most important of which is living embodiment. He the Glorified wished to embody the excess of their fear, so He showed you a picture of dry skin and a picture of upright hair. Do we not say: the hair of his head stood up out of fear? [Translator's note: the source reads «شعر رأمنه», evidently for «شعر رأسه من».] As for mentioning the skins alone first and joining them with the hearts second, it is because the mention of fear, whose place is the hearts, necessarily entails mention of the hearts. It is as though it were said: their skins shudder and their hearts fear at the beginning, but when they remember Allah and remember His mercy and its breadth, they exchange the fear for hope in their hearts and the shuddering for softness in their skins. It was also said that the meaning is: since the Qur'an is at the utmost of eloquence and rhetoric, when they saw their inability to rival it, their skins shuddered at it out of reverence for it and wonder at its beauty and eloquence, then their skins and hearts softened toward the remembrance of Allah.
